195	/// The size whose short edge is `short`, in the aspect of a `width` ×
196	/// `height` document: the long edge is `short` × the document's long edge
197	/// over its short one, rounded to the nearest even integer with a tie
198	/// going up, on the axis the document is longer along. A square document
199	/// gives `short` × `short`.
200	fn fitted((width, height): (u32, u32), short: u32) -> (u32, u32) {
201	    let doc_long = u64::from(width.max(height));
202	    // `validate` refuses a zero edge; the `max` keeps the division total
203	    // regardless, since no input may panic.
204	    let doc_short = u64::from(width.min(height)).max(1);
205	
206	    // The nearest even integer to short × doc_long / doc_short is twice
207	    // the nearest integer to half of it, and round(a / b) with a tie going
208	    // up is (2a + b) / 2b in integer division — here a = short × doc_long
209	    // and b = 2 × doc_short, so the whole thing is one division. u64
210	    // because a canvas need only be non-zero (`validate`), not inside
211	    // `set_canvas`'s 16..16384, so the product is not bounded by u32.
212	    let half = (u64::from(short) * doc_long + doc_short) / (2 * doc_short);
213	    // A canvas far outside those bounds can carry a ratio no u32 holds;
214	    // the row is then unusable, but a query must answer, and evenly.
215	    let long = u32::try_from(half * 2).unwrap_or(u32::MAX - 1);
216	
217	    if width >= height {
218	        (long, short)
219	    } else {
220	        (short, long)
221	    }
222	}

224	/// A size as a row that needs even dimensions writes it (spec §11 G-33),
225	/// each edge on its own: below 2 it is 2, an odd edge is one SMALLER, and an
226	/// even edge is itself. The rule `export_settings` and
227	/// [`Project::export_sizes`] share, so the list and the resolver cannot
228	/// disagree about what an H.264 will measure; the module doc says why down.
229	/// It is `ExporterWriter.evenDimension`'s arithmetic, which stays as the
230	/// floor under any caller that did not come through here.
231	pub(crate) fn even_size((width, height): (u32, u32)) -> (u32, u32) {
232	    let even = |edge: u32| if edge < 2 { 2 } else { edge - edge % 2 };
233	    (even(width), even(height))
234	}
235	
236	/// A `width` × `height` canvas fitted inside a box: the canvas itself when
237	/// it already fits — never upscaled — and otherwise scaled down, aspect
238	/// kept, so that the edge which meets the box first takes the box's value
239	/// exactly and the other is the scaled value rounded UP to a whole pixel.
240	/// The rule an image format's size means (module doc), shared by
241	/// `export_settings` and [`Project::export_sizes`] so the two cannot
242	/// disagree about what a GIF will measure.
243	///
244	/// Up rather than to the nearest, so that the fit is its own fixed point.
245	/// Fitting the result again compares box × canvas products on the two
246	/// axes, and the derived edge — never below its exact value — keeps the
247	/// same axis limiting, whose derived edge is the same ceiling; rounded to
248	/// the nearest it can fall below the exact value, flip the limiting axis
249	/// on the second pass, and take a pixel off the other edge (a 3024 × 1964
250	/// recording's 1080p box, 1662 × 1080, came back 1662 × 1079 and then
251	/// 1661 × 1079). The ceiling never leaves the box: the limiting axis is
252	/// the one whose exact scaled value fits, and a whole number no smaller
253	/// than a value that fits inside a whole box edge fits too.
254	pub(crate) fn fit_within((width, height): (u32, u32), (box_w, box_h): (u32, u32)) -> (u32, u32) {
255	    if width <= box_w && height <= box_h {
256	        return (width, height);
257	    }
258	    let (w, h) = (u64::from(width).max(1), u64::from(height).max(1));
259	    let (bw, bh) = (u64::from(box_w).max(1), u64::from(box_h).max(1));
260	    // The width meets the box first when box_w / w ≤ box_h / h, which is
261	    // box_w × h ≤ box_h × w with no division to round.
262	    let (fw, fh) = if bw * h <= bh * w {
263	        (bw, ceil_div(h * bw, w))
264	    } else {
265	        (ceil_div(w * bh, h), bh)
266	    };
267	    let edge = |value: u64| u32::try_from(value).unwrap_or(u32::MAX).max(1);
268	    (edge(fw), edge(fh))
269	}
270	
271	/// `a / b` rounded up to a whole number; `b ≥ 1`.
272	fn ceil_div(a: u64, b: u64) -> u64 {
273	    a.div_ceil(b)
274	}

291	/// One row of the table. Crate-visible so `export_size.rs` can read the
292	/// cap and the codec of the row it lists sizes for, and so `export.rs`'s
293	/// resolver can read the rest, both through [`preset`]; every field is
294	/// `pub(crate)` because the table's rows are built in `export_table.rs`.
295	pub(crate) struct Preset {
296	    pub(crate) id: &'static str,
297	    pub(crate) name: &'static str,
298	    pub(crate) container: Container,
299	    pub(crate) codec: &'static str,
300	    /// False for the three audio-only presets; every other row carries
301	    /// video.
302	    pub(crate) video: bool,
303	    /// Whether this ENCODING carries an alpha channel — `hevc_alpha`,
304	    /// `vp9_alpha_webm`, `prores_4444` and `apng`, and nothing else. It says what the FILE can
305	    /// hold, and never that a particular canvas is translucent:
306	    /// `export_settings`
307	    /// emits one flat object for every row, so a flag derived from the
308	    /// project's background would report `alpha: true` on an H.264, a GIF
309	    /// and a WAV, which reads as a defect from either side of the FFI. A
310	    /// transparent canvas exported through a row with no fourth channel
311	    /// simply composites onto black, and the flag is what lets the sheet
312	    /// and the `export` tool say so before the file exists.
313	    ///
314	    /// **It is a `Preset` field and not a [`Container`] question**, which
315	    /// is the one thing worth arguing here, because the neighbouring
316	    /// capability [`Container::carries_audio`] IS a container question and
317	    /// the two look alike. Whether a file can hold a sound track is decided
318	    /// by the container's format — a GIF has no audio track to put samples
319	    /// in whatever you encode — so it is answered once for the container.
320	    /// A fourth channel is decided by the CODEC: `Container::Mov` hosts
321	    /// `prores_422` and `prores_4444` alike, and 422 cannot carry alpha at
322	    /// any bitrate, so a container-level answer would have to be wrong for
323	    /// one of the two rows. Same shape of fact, different owner.
324	    ///
325	    /// **`gif` is false and `apng` is true, and the difference is the word
326	    /// CHANNEL.** Both can show a transparent pixel, so both look alike
327	    /// from the outside and a reader who has exported one will call this
328	    /// row a mistake. APNG is true colour with a real fourth channel and a
329	    /// pixel may be any fraction of opaque. A GIF has ONE palette index
330	    /// nominated as transparent: a pixel is either that index or fully
331	    /// opaque, there is no partial value to store, and a soft edge against
332	    /// nothing comes out as a hard jagged one. A flag that answered "yes"
333	    /// for both would license the sheet to promise a translucent GIF.
334	    /// Measured on the way in, not assumed: an `apng` export of a
335	    /// transparent canvas decodes `pix_fmt=rgba` with its corner at
336	    /// alpha 0, and a `gif` of the same timeline decodes with the corner
337	    /// transparent through its palette and no partial value anywhere.
338	    pub(crate) alpha: bool,
339	    /// `None` means "the project's canvas size", which is what every movie
340	    /// row wants: a preset is an encoding, and the size is the document's
341	    /// unless a `width`/`height` override says otherwise. The resolver
342	    /// fills the canvas in for the audio-only rows too, so every settings
343	    /// object carries a width. Only the two image rows pin one — the cap
344	    /// `Project::export_sizes` lists as their default.
345	    pub(crate) size: Option<(u32, u32)>,
346	    /// `None` means "the project's canvas rate", which is what every movie
347	    /// preset wants. Only the image-sequence rows pin one, because their
348	    /// cost is frames × pixels and nothing else.
349	    pub(crate) fps: Option<Fps>,
350	    /// The `AVAssetExportSession` preset name, verbatim; `None` for a
351	    /// container AVFoundation cannot write.
352	    ///
353	    /// Since phase 5 the field means only **"AVFoundation can write this
354	    /// row"**, and the name itself is a record rather than an instruction.
355	    /// Nothing has run a session since M2, but `null` here is still the
356	    /// one thing routing an export to the ImageIO writer
357	    /// (`ExportSettings.isImageSequence` is literally `avPreset == nil`),

359	    /// AVFoundation has no name for it. There is no `AVAssetExportPreset`

362	    /// available — "an audio-only file AVFoundation writes" — and a null
363	    /// there would hand a WAV to `ImageSequenceWriter`, which would refuse
364	    /// it as an unknown image container and report a format this table

366	    /// read back through AVFoundation" (spec §11 CX-15), which is all it says
367	    /// on `av1_webm` and `vp9_webm`, whose files the core writes.
368	    pub(crate) avf_preset: Option<&'static str>,
369	    /// The bundled encoder that writes the row's video, or `None` for
370	    /// AVFoundation's own encoders (ImageIO where `avf_preset` is null).
371	    /// A row with a writer takes `encoder_speed` when its encoder has
372	    /// speeds (`Writer::takes_speed`).
373	    pub(crate) writer: Option<Writer>,
374	}

381	        Some(fps) => Value::Array(vec![Value::from(fps.num), Value::from(fps.den)]),

386	impl Preset {
387	    /// True for the rows written frame by frame through ImageIO — the ones
388	    /// with no session preset — whose picture is FITTED inside the size
389	    /// rather than letterboxed to it, so a size on them is a box and the
390	    /// resolved numbers are the fit (`export_size::fit_within`).
391	    pub(crate) fn fits_inside_size(&self) -> bool {
392	        self.video && self.avf_preset.is_none()
393	    }
394	
395	    /// True for the rows whose frame has to have EVEN pixel dimensions:
396	    /// every row AVFoundation writes but ProRes 4444 (spec §11 G-33). On
397	    /// these an odd edge is resolved one pixel smaller, in the size list's
398	    /// Document row and in the resolved settings alike
399	    /// (`export_size::even_size`), so the size reported is the size the
400	    /// writer writes.
401	    ///
402	    /// It is asked of `avf_preset` and the codec rather than listed row by
403	    /// row, so a new AVFoundation row is even-sized until someone exempts
404	    /// it — the safe side, since 4:2:0 chroma needs it and a row that can
405	    /// keep an odd edge has to be measured doing so, as ProRes 4444 was
406	    /// (`ExporterWriter+Settings.swift`'s `encodedSize`). The audio-only
407	    /// rows answer true: they have no picture and go on reporting what
408	    /// `h264` reports. The two image rows answer false; their numbers are
409	    /// the fit (`fits_inside_size`), odd or not.
410	    pub(crate) fn even_sized(&self) -> bool {
411	        self.avf_preset.is_some() && self.codec != "prores4444"
412	    }
413	
414	    /// True for a row whose bundled encoder has speeds, the rows
415	    /// `encoder_speed` applies to (spec §11 CX-12 (2), CX-16 (2)).
416	    pub(crate) fn takes_encoder_speed(&self) -> bool {
417	        self.writer.is_some_and(Writer::takes_speed)
418	    }
419	
420	    /// True for the uncompressed audio rows, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`,
421	    /// the rows `audio_bits` applies to (spec §11 AU-29). ProRes's LPCM
422	    /// track keeps 16 bits; it is not an `lpcm` row.
423	    pub(crate) fn takes_audio_bits(&self) -> bool {
424	        self.codec == "lpcm"
425	    }
426	
427	    /// True for the three audio-only rows, `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav` and
428	    /// `audio_aiff`, the rows `stems` applies to (spec §11 AU-108 (a)).
429	    pub(crate) fn takes_stems(&self) -> bool {
430	        !self.video
431	    }
432	
433	    pub(crate) fn to_json(&self) -> Value {
434	        let mut out = Map::new();
435	        out.insert("id".to_string(), Value::from(self.id));
436	        out.insert("name".to_string(), Value::from(self.name));
437	        out.insert(
438	            "container".to_string(),
439	            Value::from(self.container.as_str()),
440	        );
441	        out.insert("codec".to_string(), Value::from(self.codec));
442	        out.insert("video".to_string(), Value::from(self.video));
443	        out.insert(
444	            "size".to_string(),
445	            match self.size {
446	                Some((w, h)) => Value::Array(vec![Value::from(w), Value::from(h)]),
447	                None => Value::Null,
448	            },
449	        );
450	        // `size` and `fps` are spelled the same way for the same reason:
451	        // null is "whatever the project is" — the document size, the
452	        // document rate — which the resolver fills in from the canvas.
453	        out.insert("fps".to_string(), fps_json(self.fps));
454	        out.insert(
455	            "avf_preset".to_string(),
456	            match self.avf_preset {
457	                Some(name) => Value::from(name),
458	                None => Value::Null,
459	            },
460	        );
461	        if crate::dynamic_range::HDR_ROWS.contains(&self.id) {
462	            out.insert("hdr".to_string(), Value::from(true));
463	        }
464	        if let Some(writer) = self.writer {
465	            out.insert("writer".to_string(), Value::from(writer.as_str()));
466	            if writer.takes_speed() {
467	                let speeds = EncoderSpeed::ALL.iter().map(|s| Value::from(s.as_str()));
468	                out.insert("encoder_speeds".to_string(), speeds.collect());
469	            }
470	        }
471	        if self.takes_audio_bits() {
472	            let bits = [16, 24].iter().map(|b| Value::from(*b));
473	            out.insert("audio_bits".to_string(), bits.collect());
474	        }
475	        if self.takes_stems() {
476	            let modes = ["tracks", "names"].iter().map(|m| Value::from(*m));
477	            out.insert("stems".to_string(), modes.collect());
478	        }
479	        Value::Object(out)
480	    }
481	}

491	/// The containers Frame Job writes. Kept as an enum rather than a string so
492	/// the container, its UTI, its network-optimization default and whether it
493	/// can hold sound at all are decided in exactly one exhaustive place.
494	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
495	pub(crate) enum Container {
496	    Mov,
497	    Mp4,
498	    M4a,
499	    Wav,
500	    Aiff,
501	    Gif,
502	    Apng,
503	    /// WebM, written by the core's own writer (`webm_writer.rs`, spec §11
504	    /// CX-15), not by AVFoundation.
505	    Webm,
506	}

508	impl Container {
509	    pub(crate) fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
510	        match self {
511	            Container::Mov => "mov",
512	            Container::Mp4 => "mp4",
513	            Container::M4a => "m4a",
514	            Container::Wav => "wav",
515	            Container::Aiff => "aiff",
516	            Container::Gif => "gif",
517	            Container::Apng => "apng",
518	            Container::Webm => "webm",
519	        }
520	    }

522	    /// The output file's UTI. On the AVFoundation path Swift passes this
523	    /// straight to `outputFileType`, whose raw values ARE UTIs; on the
524	    /// ImageIO path it is the destination type
525	    /// `CGImageDestinationCreateWithURL` takes. Either way it is what the
526	    /// save panel's content type and file extension are derived from, which
527	    /// is why the two image formats name a real UTI here rather than
528	    /// nothing — an export that could not tell the panel it writes a `.gif`
529	    /// would be worse off than one whose type string a session would
530	    /// reject, and a session is never built for them.
531	    ///
532	    /// An APNG is written to an ordinary PNG destination — the animation
533	    /// lives in `acTL`/`fcTL` chunks inside a file that is still a PNG — so
534	    /// its type identifier is PNG's, not one of its own.
535	    ///
536	    /// The two LPCM rows' identifiers are exactly `AVFileType.wav` and
537	    /// `AVFileType.aiff`'s raw values, which is what lets
538	    /// `Exporter.fileType(for:)` resolve them from this string alone
539	    /// rather than growing a container list of its own.
540	    pub(crate) fn file_type(self) -> &'static str {
541	        match self {
542	            Container::Mov => "com.apple.quicktime-movie",
543	            Container::Mp4 => "public.mpeg-4",
544	            Container::M4a => "com.apple.m4a-audio",
545	            Container::Wav => "com.microsoft.waveform-audio",
546	            Container::Aiff => "public.aiff-audio",
547	            Container::Gif => "com.compuserve.gif",
548	            Container::Apng => "public.png",
549	            Container::Webm => "org.webmproject.webm",
550	        }
551	    }
552	
553	    /// Whether `shouldOptimizeForNetworkUse` defaults on. MP4 and M4A are
554	    /// the delivery containers people upload, and a leading `moov` atom
555	    /// lets a player start before the file is fully fetched. A ProRes MOV
556	    /// is an editing master handed to another application, where the
557	    /// rewrite pass buys nothing. An HEVC-with-alpha MOV is a delivery file
558	    /// too, and its default stays off all the same: that was the owner's
559	    /// choice for the row (spec §11 G-33), and the override turns it on. GIF
560	    /// and APNG have no `moov` atom and nothing to move: a viewer already
561	    /// starts on the first frame, and
562	    /// neither do WAV and AIFF — a RIFF or an IFF file is a header
563	    /// followed by samples, with no index to relocate, so the flag would

648	//! How an export override is READ and REFUSED — the vocabulary the export
649	//! settings resolve from, where `export_table.rs` is the table and
650	//! `export.rs` the resolution.
651	//!
652	//! Cut out of `export.rs` in road map 2's phase 5, and cut HERE for the
653	//! reason `props_check.rs` was cut out of `edit_props.rs`: a rule about
654	//! how a value is spelled and what makes it a refusal is a fact about the
655	//! VOCABULARY, not about the resolution. Nothing in this file knows which
656	//! preset asked, what the canvas is, or what the settings object ends up
657	//! looking like; everything in it answers one question — "is this JSON
658	//! value a legal `width` / `fps` / `range` / bitrate / decibel figure, and
659	//! if not, what do we tell the caller it was?".
660	//!
661	//! The cut also paid the size rule's toll. `export.rs` stood at 578 lines
662	//! against the ~600 soft cap and phase 5 added two containers, two preset
663	//! rows, a decibel validator, two override reads and two echo lines; a
664	//! file at the line gives something up before it takes anything on.
665	//!
666	//! Three rules hold for every reader here, and every new one must keep
667	//! them, because the sheet, the `export` tool and the test suite all lean
668	//! on them:
669	//!
670	//! 1. **Absent and explicit null are the same thing** — "use the preset".
671	//!    That is what lets the export sheet build one overrides object and
672	//!    null the fields whose control is greyed out.
673	//! 2. **An unknown key is ignored, silently.** A newer UI may send fields
674	//!    this build has never heard of and must still get an export.
675	//! 3. **A refusal names the offending value**, through [`describe`], and
676	//!    the message is lowercase and starts `export <key> must be …`. The
677	//!    key is in the message because a caller sending six overrides needs
678	//!    to know which one it was.
679	//!
680	//! [`describe`] itself is not about export at all any more: five modules
681	//! outside this one (`edit.rs`, `edit_props.rs`, `edit_action.rs`,
682	//! `edit_paste.rs`, `edit_track.rs`) name it `crate::export::describe` for
683	//! their own error messages, so `export.rs` re-exports it under that path
684	//! and the cut costs those files nothing. [`spelled`] sits beside it for
685	//! the same reason: a vocabulary value's own JSON spelling, for a sentence
686	//! (`lut.rs`, `media_color.rs`, `edit_relink.rs`).
687	
688	use serde_json::Value;
689	
690	use crate::dynamic_range::DynamicRange;
691	use crate::export_table::EncoderSpeed;
692	use crate::time::{Fps, Ticks};

696	/// A JSON value as short text for an error message, truncated on a char
697	/// boundary so a pasted megabyte of JSON cannot become the error string.
698	pub(crate) fn describe(value: &Value) -> String {
699	    let text = value.to_string();
700	    if text.chars().count() <= 40 {
701	        text
702	    } else {
703	        format!("{} …", text.chars().take(40).collect::<String>())
704	    }
705	}

707	/// A vocabulary value's JSON spelling (`warm`, `video`), serde's own, so a
708	/// sentence names it as the file and the schema do.
709	pub(crate) fn spelled<T: serde::Serialize>(value: T) -> String {
710	    serde_json::to_value(value)
711	        .ok()
712	        .and_then(|value| value.as_str().map(str::to_string))
713	        .unwrap_or_default()
714	}

716	/// The overrides object itself: `None` for absent, null or an empty
717	/// request, `Some` for an object, and an `Err` naming the value for
718	/// anything else. One place, so "overrides must be a json object" is the
719	/// same sentence however the caller got here.
720	pub(crate) fn object(overrides: Option<&Value>) -> Result<Option<&Value>, String> {
721	    match overrides {
722	        None => Ok(None),
723	        Some(Value::Null) => Ok(None),
724	        Some(value) if value.is_object() => Ok(Some(value)),
725	        Some(value) => Err(format!(
726	            "export overrides must be a json object, not {}",
727	            describe(value)
728	        )),
729	    }
730	}

732	/// An override field, or `None` when absent or explicitly null (null means
733	/// "use the preset", so a caller can build one overrides object and leave
734	/// the fields it does not care about).
735	fn field<'a>(overrides: Option<&'a Value>, key: &str) -> Option<&'a Value> {
736	    overrides.and_then(|o| o.get(key)).filter(|v| !v.is_null())
737	}

740	
741	/// A strictly positive integer override — the pixel dimensions and the two
742	/// bitrates, which want the identical check. `u64::MAX` is not the ceiling
743	/// on purpose: a bitrate is bits per second, and `u32`'s 4.3 Gbit/s is an
744	/// order of magnitude past anything deliverable (ProRes 422 at 4K is about
745	/// 0.7), so the same bound that keeps a width sane keeps a bitrate honest.
746	/// Zero and negative both land in the error arm, which names the value.
747	pub(crate) fn positive_u32(overrides: Option<&Value>, key: &str) -> Result<Option<u32>, String> {
748	    let Some(value) = field(overrides, key) else {
749	        return Ok(None);
750	    };
751	    match value.as_u64() {
752	        Some(n) if n > 0 && n <= u64::from(u32::MAX) => Ok(Some(n as u32)),
753	        _ => Err(format!(
754	            "export {key} must be a positive integer, not {}",
755	            describe(value)
756	        )),
757	    }
758	}

760	/// A decibel override: a finite number inside `[min, max]`. The f64 twin
761	/// of [`positive_u32`], and a separate function because the two loudness
762	/// figures are NEGATIVE FRACTIONS — −14.5 LUFS is a real request — so
763	/// every guard `positive_u32` applies is the wrong one here.
764	///
765	/// `as_f64` is the whole type check: `serde_json` answers `None` for a
766	/// bool, a string, an array and an object alike, so the error arm catches
767	/// them all and names what arrived. Non-finite is checked even though JSON
768	/// cannot spell a NaN or an infinity — the function takes a `Value` from
769	/// whoever has one, and a bound comparison against a NaN is silently false
770	/// rather than an error.
771	fn decibels(
772	    overrides: Option<&Value>,
773	    key: &str,
774	    min: f64,
775	    max: f64,
776	) -> Result<Option<f64>, String> {
777	    let Some(value) = field(overrides, key) else {
778	        return Ok(None);
779	    };
780	    match value.as_f64() {
781	        Some(db) if db.is_finite() && db >= min && db <= max => Ok(Some(db)),
782	        _ => Err(format!(
783	            "export {key} must be a number from {min} to {max}, not {}",
784	            describe(value)
785	        )),
786	    }
787	}
788	
789	/// The bottom of the loudness target's range. −70 LUFS is BS.1770-4's own
790	/// absolute gate: a programme quieter than that measures as nothing at
791	/// all, so a target at or below it is a request the measurement cannot
792	/// even express. The top is 0 LUFS — full scale, unwise but legal, and the
793	/// bound is where it is so the message is about the value.
794	const LOUDNESS_MIN: f64 = -70.0;
795	const LOUDNESS_MAX: f64 = 0.0;
796	
797	/// The true-peak ceiling's range. 0 dBTP is legal (and what a master with
798	/// no headroom asks for); −20 is far below anything a deliverable wants
799	/// and exists only so a mistyped LUFS figure lands in the error arm rather
800	/// than turning the programme down by 60 dB.
801	const PEAK_MIN: f64 = -20.0;
802	const PEAK_MAX: f64 = 0.0;
803	
804	/// The two loudness overrides, read together: `loudness_lufs`, the
805	/// integrated target the export is normalised to, and `peak_dbtp`, the
806	/// true-peak ceiling of the export's master limiter.
807	///
808	/// **Either may come alone** (spec §11 AU-27). Every export with sound runs
809	/// through a master limiter at `peak_dbtp`, −1 dBTP when it is not asked
810	/// for, so a ceiling on its own is not inert: it is the limiter's ceiling,
811	/// with or without a target, and is accepted and echoed as every other
812	/// override is.
813	///
814	/// Both are emitted by the resolver only when asked for, exactly as the
815	/// bitrates are: an absent `loudness_lufs` is "do not normalise", which is
816	/// what `ExportSettings.loudnessLufs == nil` says on the Swift side, and an
817	/// absent `peak_dbtp` is the master's default ceiling there.
818	pub(crate) fn loudness(overrides: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(Option<f64>, Option<f64>), String> {
819	    let target = decibels(overrides, "loudness_lufs", LOUDNESS_MIN, LOUDNESS_MAX)?;
820	    let ceiling = decibels(overrides, "peak_dbtp", PEAK_MIN, PEAK_MAX)?;
821	    Ok((target, ceiling))
822	}

917	/// The `fps` override as `[num, den]`, or `default` when it is absent.
918	/// Both terms are read as `u64` and bounded by `u32::MAX` because that is
919	/// what [`Fps`] holds, and both must be non-zero: a zero numerator is a
920	/// frozen export and a zero denominator is a division by nothing, and
921	/// either would reach the frame-snapping arithmetic before anyone noticed.
922	pub(crate) fn fps(overrides: Option<&Value>, default: Fps) -> Result<Fps, String> {
923	    let Some(value) = field(overrides, "fps") else {
924	        return Ok(default);
925	    };
926	    let terms = value.as_array().and_then(|a| {
927	        match (
928	            a.first().and_then(Value::as_u64),
929	            a.get(1).and_then(Value::as_u64),
930	        ) {
931	            (Some(num), Some(den)) if a.len() == 2 => Some((num, den)),
932	            _ => None,
933	        }
934	    });
935	    match terms {
936	        Some((num, den))
937	            if num > 0 && den > 0 && num <= u64::from(u32::MAX) && den <= u64::from(u32::MAX) =>
938	        {
939	            Ok(Fps {
940	                num: num as u32,
941	                den: den as u32,
942	            })
943	        }
944	        _ => Err(format!(
945	            "export fps must be [num, den] with non-zero terms, not {}",
946	            describe(value)
947	        )),
948	    }
949	}

955	            "export {what} must be an integer number of ticks, not {}",

961	/// The `range` override as the raw `(start, duration)` pair it asked for,
962	/// each falling back to its half of `default` — which is `(0, the whole
963	/// project)`, so `{"start": …}` alone keeps the project's length and
964	/// `{"duration": …}` alone keeps its start.
965	///
966	/// RAW is the word: nothing here snaps or clamps. Both are decisions about
967	/// a project and an export rate, which this file knows nothing about, and
968	/// the ORDER of the two (snap first, then clamp) is load-bearing enough to
969	/// stay visible where the settings are resolved.
970	pub(crate) fn range(
971	    overrides: Option<&Value>,
972	    default: (Ticks, Ticks),
973	) -> Result<(Ticks, Ticks), String> {
974	    let Some(range) = field(overrides, "range") else {
975	        return Ok(default);
976	    };
977	    if !range.is_object() {
978	        return Err(format!(
979	            "export range must be a json object with start and duration, not {}",
980	            describe(range)
981	        ));
982	    }
983	    let (mut start, mut duration) = default;
984	    if let Some(value) = field(Some(range), "start") {
985	        start = ticks(value, "range start")?;
986	    }
987	    if let Some(value) = field(Some(range), "duration") {
988	        duration = ticks(value, "range duration")?;
989	    }
990	    Ok((start, duration))
991	}

1	//! The output sizes the export sheet offers for one document and one
2	//! format — `rc_export_sizes` (spec §7.8) — and the one rule for what a
3	//! size MEANS on an image format, which `export_settings` applies too.
4	//!
5	//! A preset is an encoding and carries no size (`export.rs`), so the size
6	//! is a second choice, and this module is the list that choice is made
7	//! from: the format's cap if it has one, the document's own size, and the
8	//! standard sizes fitted to the document's aspect. The FIRST row is the
9	//! default — the rule every list the export sheet is built from follows —
10	//! which is the document's size for a movie format and the cap for an
11	//! image format, because an image format's cap is the point of the row
12	//! and not a ceiling that only applies from above.
13	//!
14	//! **The number is the short edge.** A standard size is named by one
15	//! number, and the number people use is the short one: "1080p ultrawide"
16	//! is 2560 × 1080 and "1080p vertical" is 1080 × 1920, and both are 1080p
17	//! to everyone who says it. Naming by the long edge would call the
18	//! ultrawide 2560p and the vertical 1920p, which nobody does. So a row
19	//! keeps its short edge exactly and the long edge follows the document:
20	//! L = S × long / short of the document, on whichever axis the document is
21	//! longer along, and S × S for a square.
22	//!
23	//! **The long edge is rounded to even.** 4:2:0 chroma puts one colour
24	//! sample under each 2 × 2 block of luma, so H.264 and HEVC want even
25	//! dimensions, and `ExporterWriter.evenDimension` rounds an odd one down
26	//! before writing. Rounding here — to the nearest even integer, a tie
27	//! going up — means the size the popup shows is the size the file has;
28	//! leaving it to the writer would change the size behind the sheet's
29	//! back.
30	//!
31	//! **The even rule (spec §11 G-33).** The same is true of the document row
32	//! and of any size asked for, so on every row that needs even dimensions
33	//! (`Preset::even_sized`: every row AVFoundation writes but ProRes 4444)
34	//! the size is resolved HERE, by [`even_size`]: the document row's numbers
35	//! in this list, and in `export_settings` whatever was asked. An odd edge
36	//! is one pixel SMALLER. Down, because that is the size the writer already
37	//! wrote, so the report moves to the file and no file changes size;
38	//! because rounding up would hand the encoder a frame larger than the
39	//! picture on that axis; and because every listed row is then its own
40	//! fixed point, as an image format's is. The row is named "Document
41	//! (even)" when its numbers are not the canvas's, which is the whole of
42	//! how the popup says why. The argument this replaces was that a "Document
43	//! size" that was not the document's size would be a lie; the lie was the
44	//! row that said 321 × 181 over a file of 320 × 180. ProRes 4444 and the
45	//! two image formats keep an odd edge, and their row is "Document size",
46	//! the canvas as it is.
47	//!
48	//! **An image format's numbers are the file's.** A GIF or an APNG is
49	//! written frame by frame with the picture FITTED inside the size — aspect
50	//! kept, never upscaled — where a movie is letterboxed to exactly the frame
51	//! asked for (`ExporterImageSequence`, spec §7.8): padding costs bytes in
52	//! every frame for pixels that carry nothing, and a bigger frame carries no
53	//! more detail. So on those two formats every row here, and every size
54	//! `export_settings` resolves — the cap, a standard row, a custom size — is
55	//! the canvas fitted inside that box ([`fit_within`]), so that the popup,
56	//! the sheet's readout and the `export` tool all report the numbers the
57	//! file will have: a vertical 1080 × 1920 timeline's "GIF default" is
58	//! 152 × 270, not 480 × 270. The fit is decided here, once; the writer
59	//! draws each frame at exactly this size and does not fit a second time.
60	//! It is also its own fixed point — a fitted size fed back as the box
61	//! fits to itself — because that is exactly what happens: the sheet and
62	//! the tool send a listed row's numbers back through `export_settings` as
63	//! `width` and `height`, and a fit that could move a derived edge by a
64	//! pixel on the second pass would show one size and write another.
65	//!
66	//! **Rows may repeat.** A 1920 × 1080 document's 1080p row IS the document
67	//! row, and on a 1080 × 1920 document every image-format row from 1080p up
68	//! is the document again. They are listed anyway, because an id is the
69	//! `export` tool's vocabulary and a request for `1080p` has to mean the
70	//! same thing on every document — refusing it exactly where it is a no-op
71	//! would be the popup's tidiness leaking into an API. The sheet hides a
72	//! row whose numbers an earlier row already has, so a person never sees one
73	//! size under two names, and the row that shows is the one whose name says
74	//! more ("Document size" over "1080p"). Rows larger than the document are
75	//! offered for a movie — they were before, as the 4K preset — because a
76	//! 720p screen recording exported at 4K for a platform that picks its
77	//! bitrate by resolution is a real request.
78

82	use crate::model::Project;

84	/// The standard sizes, largest first, as (id, name, short edge). The id is
85	/// the `export` tool's vocabulary and the name is the popup's; they differ
86	/// only for 4K, which nobody calls 2160p out loud but which needs a
87	/// short-edge id to sit in the same vocabulary as the other three.
88	const STANDARD: [(&str, &str, u32); 4] = [
89	    ("2160p", "4K", 2160),
90	    ("1440p", "1440p", 1440),
91	    ("1080p", "1080p", 1080),
92	    ("720p", "720p", 720),
93	];

95	/// One row of the list, before it is JSON.

115	    /// The sizes the export sheet offers for `preset_id` against this
116	    /// document, as the JSON array of `{id, name, width, height}` rows
117	    /// `rc_export_sizes` returns, in menu order — the first is the default.
118	    ///
119	    /// The rows:
120	    ///
121	    /// 1. `preset` — the format's cap, "GIF default" / "APNG default", for
122	    ///    the two rows of the table that carry one; nothing for the rest.
123	    /// 2. `document` — "Document size", the canvas as it is; on a row that
124	    ///    needs even dimensions the canvas evened ([`even_size`]), named
125	    ///    "Document (even)" when that is not the canvas's own size.
126	    /// 3. `2160p` ("4K"), `1440p`, `1080p`, `720p` — the short edge named,
127	    ///    the long edge fitted to the canvas and rounded to even.
128	    ///
129	    /// On an image format every row's numbers are the canvas fitted inside
130	    /// that row's box, never upscaled — the size the file will have. Rows
131	    /// may repeat an earlier row's numbers and are listed anyway (the
132	    /// module doc says why); the sheet hides the repeats.
133	    ///
134	    /// One list for every movie format, the audio-only row included: a
135	    /// width is reported for it the way `export_settings` reports one, and
136	    /// the sheet disables the control rather than this module keeping a
137	    /// second rule for one row. `Err` for an unknown preset, naming it —
138	    /// the same lookup and the same words as `export_settings`.
139	    pub fn export_sizes(&self, preset_id: &str) -> Result<Value, String> {
140	        let preset = export::preset(preset_id)?;
141	        let document = (self.canvas.width, self.canvas.height);
142	        let fits = preset.fits_inside_size();
143	        let sized = |(width, height): (u32, u32)| {
144	            if fits {
145	                fit_within(document, (width, height))
146	            } else {
147	                (width, height)
148	            }
149	        };
150	
151	        let mut rows: Vec<Row> = Vec::new();
152	        if let Some(cap) = preset.size {
153	            // The codec in capitals is the format's name as people write
154	            // it — GIF, APNG — for the two rows that carry a cap.
155	            let (width, height) = sized(cap);
156	            rows.push(Row {
157	                id: "preset",
158	                name: format!("{} default", preset.codec.to_uppercase()),
159	                width,
160	                height,
161	            });
162	        }
163	        // The id is `document` either way: the name is the popup's, and it
164	        // changes only when the numbers are not the canvas's.
165	        let listed = if preset.even_sized() {
166	            even_size(document)
167	        } else {
168	            document
169	        };
170	        let name = if listed == document {
171	            "Document size"
172	        } else {
173	            "Document (even)"
174	        };
175	        rows.push(Row {
176	            id: "document",
177	            name: name.to_string(),
178	            width: listed.0,
179	            height: listed.1,
180	        });
181	        for (id, name, short) in STANDARD {
182	            let (width, height) = sized(fitted(document, short));
183	            rows.push(Row {
184	                id,
185	                name: name.to_string(),
186	                width,
187	                height,
188	            });
189	        }
190	
191	        Ok(Value::Array(rows.iter().map(Row::to_json).collect()))
192	    }
193	}

195	/// The size whose short edge is `short`, in the aspect of a `width` ×
196	/// `height` document: the long edge is `short` × the document's long edge
197	/// over its short one, rounded to the nearest even integer with a tie
198	/// going up, on the axis the document is longer along. A square document
199	/// gives `short` × `short`.
200	fn fitted((width, height): (u32, u32), short: u32) -> (u32, u32) {
201	    let doc_long = u64::from(width.max(height));
202	    // `validate` refuses a zero edge; the `max` keeps the division total
203	    // regardless, since no input may panic.
204	    let doc_short = u64::from(width.min(height)).max(1);
205	
206	    // The nearest even integer to short × doc_long / doc_short is twice
207	    // the nearest integer to half of it, and round(a / b) with a tie going
208	    // up is (2a + b) / 2b in integer division — here a = short × doc_long
209	    // and b = 2 × doc_short, so the whole thing is one division. u64
210	    // because a canvas need only be non-zero (`validate`), not inside
211	    // `set_canvas`'s 16..16384, so the product is not bounded by u32.
212	    let half = (u64::from(short) * doc_long + doc_short) / (2 * doc_short);
213	    // A canvas far outside those bounds can carry a ratio no u32 holds;
214	    // the row is then unusable, but a query must answer, and evenly.
215	    let long = u32::try_from(half * 2).unwrap_or(u32::MAX - 1);
216	
217	    if width >= height {
218	        (long, short)
219	    } else {
220	        (short, long)
221	    }
222	}

224	/// A size as a row that needs even dimensions writes it (spec §11 G-33),
225	/// each edge on its own: below 2 it is 2, an odd edge is one SMALLER, and an
226	/// even edge is itself. The rule `export_settings` and
227	/// [`Project::export_sizes`] share, so the list and the resolver cannot
228	/// disagree about what an H.264 will measure; the module doc says why down.
229	/// It is `ExporterWriter.evenDimension`'s arithmetic, which stays as the
230	/// floor under any caller that did not come through here.
231	pub(crate) fn even_size((width, height): (u32, u32)) -> (u32, u32) {
232	    let even = |edge: u32| if edge < 2 { 2 } else { edge - edge % 2 };
233	    (even(width), even(height))
234	}
235	
236	/// A `width` × `height` canvas fitted inside a box: the canvas itself when
237	/// it already fits — never upscaled — and otherwise scaled down, aspect
238	/// kept, so that the edge which meets the box first takes the box's value
239	/// exactly and the other is the scaled value rounded UP to a whole pixel.
240	/// The rule an image format's size means (module doc), shared by
241	/// `export_settings` and [`Project::export_sizes`] so the two cannot
242	/// disagree about what a GIF will measure.
243	///
244	/// Up rather than to the nearest, so that the fit is its own fixed point.
245	/// Fitting the result again compares box × canvas products on the two
246	/// axes, and the derived edge — never below its exact value — keeps the
247	/// same axis limiting, whose derived edge is the same ceiling; rounded to
248	/// the nearest it can fall below the exact value, flip the limiting axis
249	/// on the second pass, and take a pixel off the other edge (a 3024 × 1964
250	/// recording's 1080p box, 1662 × 1080, came back 1662 × 1079 and then
251	/// 1661 × 1079). The ceiling never leaves the box: the limiting axis is
252	/// the one whose exact scaled value fits, and a whole number no smaller
253	/// than a value that fits inside a whole box edge fits too.
254	pub(crate) fn fit_within((width, height): (u32, u32), (box_w, box_h): (u32, u32)) -> (u32, u32) {
255	    if width <= box_w && height <= box_h {
256	        return (width, height);
257	    }
258	    let (w, h) = (u64::from(width).max(1), u64::from(height).max(1));
259	    let (bw, bh) = (u64::from(box_w).max(1), u64::from(box_h).max(1));
260	    // The width meets the box first when box_w / w ≤ box_h / h, which is
261	    // box_w × h ≤ box_h × w with no division to round.
262	    let (fw, fh) = if bw * h <= bh * w {
263	        (bw, ceil_div(h * bw, w))
264	    } else {
265	        (ceil_div(w * bh, h), bh)
266	    };
267	    let edge = |value: u64| u32::try_from(value).unwrap_or(u32::MAX).max(1);
268	    (edge(fw), edge(fh))
269	}
270	
271	/// `a / b` rounded up to a whole number; `b ≥ 1`.
272	fn ceil_div(a: u64, b: u64) -> u64 {
273	    a.div_ceil(b)
274	}

291	/// One row of the table. Crate-visible so `export_size.rs` can read the
292	/// cap and the codec of the row it lists sizes for, and so `export.rs`'s
293	/// resolver can read the rest, both through [`preset`]; every field is
294	/// `pub(crate)` because the table's rows are built in `export_table.rs`.
295	pub(crate) struct Preset {
296	    pub(crate) id: &'static str,
297	    pub(crate) name: &'static str,
298	    pub(crate) container: Container,
299	    pub(crate) codec: &'static str,
300	    /// False for the three audio-only presets; every other row carries
301	    /// video.
302	    pub(crate) video: bool,
303	    /// Whether this ENCODING carries an alpha channel — `hevc_alpha`,
304	    /// `vp9_alpha_webm`, `prores_4444` and `apng`, and nothing else. It says what the FILE can
305	    /// hold, and never that a particular canvas is translucent:
306	    /// `export_settings`
307	    /// emits one flat object for every row, so a flag derived from the
308	    /// project's background would report `alpha: true` on an H.264, a GIF
309	    /// and a WAV, which reads as a defect from either side of the FFI. A
310	    /// transparent canvas exported through a row with no fourth channel
311	    /// simply composites onto black, and the flag is what lets the sheet
312	    /// and the `export` tool say so before the file exists.
313	    ///
314	    /// **It is a `Preset` field and not a [`Container`] question**, which
315	    /// is the one thing worth arguing here, because the neighbouring
316	    /// capability [`Container::carries_audio`] IS a container question and
317	    /// the two look alike. Whether a file can hold a sound track is decided
318	    /// by the container's format — a GIF has no audio track to put samples
319	    /// in whatever you encode — so it is answered once for the container.
320	    /// A fourth channel is decided by the CODEC: `Container::Mov` hosts
321	    /// `prores_422` and `prores_4444` alike, and 422 cannot carry alpha at
322	    /// any bitrate, so a container-level answer would have to be wrong for
323	    /// one of the two rows. Same shape of fact, different owner.
324	    ///
325	    /// **`gif` is false and `apng` is true, and the difference is the word
326	    /// CHANNEL.** Both can show a transparent pixel, so both look alike
327	    /// from the outside and a reader who has exported one will call this
328	    /// row a mistake. APNG is true colour with a real fourth channel and a
329	    /// pixel may be any fraction of opaque. A GIF has ONE palette index
330	    /// nominated as transparent: a pixel is either that index or fully
331	    /// opaque, there is no partial value to store, and a soft edge against
332	    /// nothing comes out as a hard jagged one. A flag that answered "yes"
333	    /// for both would license the sheet to promise a translucent GIF.
334	    /// Measured on the way in, not assumed: an `apng` export of a
335	    /// transparent canvas decodes `pix_fmt=rgba` with its corner at
336	    /// alpha 0, and a `gif` of the same timeline decodes with the corner
337	    /// transparent through its palette and no partial value anywhere.
338	    pub(crate) alpha: bool,
339	    /// `None` means "the project's canvas size", which is what every movie
340	    /// row wants: a preset is an encoding, and the size is the document's
341	    /// unless a `width`/`height` override says otherwise. The resolver
342	    /// fills the canvas in for the audio-only rows too, so every settings
343	    /// object carries a width. Only the two image rows pin one — the cap
344	    /// `Project::export_sizes` lists as their default.
345	    pub(crate) size: Option<(u32, u32)>,
346	    /// `None` means "the project's canvas rate", which is what every movie
347	    /// preset wants. Only the image-sequence rows pin one, because their
348	    /// cost is frames × pixels and nothing else.
349	    pub(crate) fps: Option<Fps>,
350	    /// The `AVAssetExportSession` preset name, verbatim; `None` for a
351	    /// container AVFoundation cannot write.
352	    ///
353	    /// Since phase 5 the field means only **"AVFoundation can write this
354	    /// row"**, and the name itself is a record rather than an instruction.
355	    /// Nothing has run a session since M2, but `null` here is still the
356	    /// one thing routing an export to the ImageIO writer
357	    /// (`ExportSettings.isImageSequence` is literally `avPreset == nil`),
358	    /// so a row that AVFoundation writes must carry SOME name even when
359	    /// AVFoundation has no name for it. There is no `AVAssetExportPreset`
360	    /// for LPCM in a WAV or an AIFF, so those two rows carry the audio-only
361	    /// name `audio_m4a` carries: it is the closest true statement
362	    /// available — "an audio-only file AVFoundation writes" — and a null
363	    /// there would hand a WAV to `ImageSequenceWriter`, which would refuse
364	    /// it as an unknown image container and report a format this table
365	    /// advertises as unsupported. A name also means "the composition is
366	    /// read back through AVFoundation" (spec §11 CX-15), which is all it says
367	    /// on `av1_webm` and `vp9_webm`, whose files the core writes.
368	    pub(crate) avf_preset: Option<&'static str>,
369	    /// The bundled encoder that writes the row's video, or `None` for
370	    /// AVFoundation's own encoders (ImageIO where `avf_preset` is null).
371	    /// A row with a writer takes `encoder_speed` when its encoder has
372	    /// speeds (`Writer::takes_speed`).
373	    pub(crate) writer: Option<Writer>,
374	}

376	/// A rate as the two-element `[num, den]` array the spec spells every rate
377	/// with, or null for "the project's own". One function so the preset row
378	/// and the resolved settings cannot disagree about the shape.
379	pub(crate) fn fps_json(fps: Option<Fps>) -> Value {
380	    match fps {
381	        Some(fps) => Value::Array(vec![Value::from(fps.num), Value::from(fps.den)]),
382	        None => Value::Null,

386	impl Preset {
387	    /// True for the rows written frame by frame through ImageIO — the ones
388	    /// with no session preset — whose picture is FITTED inside the size
389	    /// rather than letterboxed to it, so a size on them is a box and the
390	    /// resolved numbers are the fit (`export_size::fit_within`).
391	    pub(crate) fn fits_inside_size(&self) -> bool {
392	        self.video && self.avf_preset.is_none()
393	    }
394	
395	    /// True for the rows whose frame has to have EVEN pixel dimensions:
396	    /// every row AVFoundation writes but ProRes 4444 (spec §11 G-33). On
397	    /// these an odd edge is resolved one pixel smaller, in the size list's
398	    /// Document row and in the resolved settings alike
399	    /// (`export_size::even_size`), so the size reported is the size the
400	    /// writer writes.
401	    ///
402	    /// It is asked of `avf_preset` and the codec rather than listed row by
403	    /// row, so a new AVFoundation row is even-sized until someone exempts
404	    /// it — the safe side, since 4:2:0 chroma needs it and a row that can
405	    /// keep an odd edge has to be measured doing so, as ProRes 4444 was
406	    /// (`ExporterWriter+Settings.swift`'s `encodedSize`). The audio-only
407	    /// rows answer true: they have no picture and go on reporting what
408	    /// `h264` reports. The two image rows answer false; their numbers are
409	    /// the fit (`fits_inside_size`), odd or not.
410	    pub(crate) fn even_sized(&self) -> bool {
411	        self.avf_preset.is_some() && self.codec != "prores4444"
412	    }
413	
414	    /// True for a row whose bundled encoder has speeds, the rows
415	    /// `encoder_speed` applies to (spec §11 CX-12 (2), CX-16 (2)).
416	    pub(crate) fn takes_encoder_speed(&self) -> bool {
417	        self.writer.is_some_and(Writer::takes_speed)
418	    }
419	
420	    /// True for the uncompressed audio rows, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`,
421	    /// the rows `audio_bits` applies to (spec §11 AU-29). ProRes's LPCM
422	    /// track keeps 16 bits; it is not an `lpcm` row.
423	    pub(crate) fn takes_audio_bits(&self) -> bool {
424	        self.codec == "lpcm"
425	    }
426	
427	    /// True for the three audio-only rows, `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav` and
428	    /// `audio_aiff`, the rows `stems` applies to (spec §11 AU-108 (a)).
429	    pub(crate) fn takes_stems(&self) -> bool {
430	        !self.video
431	    }
432	
433	    pub(crate) fn to_json(&self) -> Value {
434	        let mut out = Map::new();
435	        out.insert("id".to_string(), Value::from(self.id));
436	        out.insert("name".to_string(), Value::from(self.name));
437	        out.insert(
438	            "container".to_string(),
439	            Value::from(self.container.as_str()),
440	        );
441	        out.insert("codec".to_string(), Value::from(self.codec));
442	        out.insert("video".to_string(), Value::from(self.video));
443	        out.insert(
444	            "size".to_string(),
445	            match self.size {
446	                Some((w, h)) => Value::Array(vec![Value::from(w), Value::from(h)]),
447	                None => Value::Null,
448	            },
449	        );
450	        // `size` and `fps` are spelled the same way for the same reason:
451	        // null is "whatever the project is" — the document size, the
452	        // document rate — which the resolver fills in from the canvas.
453	        out.insert("fps".to_string(), fps_json(self.fps));
454	        out.insert(
455	            "avf_preset".to_string(),
456	            match self.avf_preset {
457	                Some(name) => Value::from(name),
458	                None => Value::Null,
459	            },
460	        );
461	        if crate::dynamic_range::HDR_ROWS.contains(&self.id) {
462	            out.insert("hdr".to_string(), Value::from(true));
463	        }
464	        if let Some(writer) = self.writer {
465	            out.insert("writer".to_string(), Value::from(writer.as_str()));
466	            if writer.takes_speed() {
467	                let speeds = EncoderSpeed::ALL.iter().map(|s| Value::from(s.as_str()));
468	                out.insert("encoder_speeds".to_string(), speeds.collect());
469	            }
470	        }
471	        if self.takes_audio_bits() {
472	            let bits = [16, 24].iter().map(|b| Value::from(*b));
473	            out.insert("audio_bits".to_string(), bits.collect());
474	        }
475	        if self.takes_stems() {
476	            let modes = ["tracks", "names"].iter().map(|m| Value::from(*m));
477	            out.insert("stems".to_string(), modes.collect());
478	        }
479	        Value::Object(out)
480	    }
481	}
482	//! The containers Frame Job writes (spec §7.8), and the four questions
483	//! each one answers about ITSELF: its extension, its UTI, whether a
484	//! leading index is worth rewriting, whether it can hold sound at all.
485	//!
486	//! Moved whole out of `export_table.rs` under the size rule (core/CLAUDE.md:
487	//! a module at ~600 lines gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on),
488	//! as codec-export C1's toll T1, a pure move. `export_table.rs` re-exports
489	//! [`Container`], so every `crate::export_table::Container` path holds.
490	
491	/// The containers Frame Job writes. Kept as an enum rather than a string so
492	/// the container, its UTI, its network-optimization default and whether it
493	/// can hold sound at all are decided in exactly one exhaustive place.
494	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
495	pub(crate) enum Container {
496	    Mov,
497	    Mp4,
498	    M4a,
499	    Wav,
500	    Aiff,
501	    Gif,
502	    Apng,
503	    /// WebM, written by the core's own writer (`webm_writer.rs`, spec §11
504	    /// CX-15), not by AVFoundation.
505	    Webm,
506	}
507	
508	impl Container {
509	    pub(crate) fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
510	        match self {
511	            Container::Mov => "mov",
512	            Container::Mp4 => "mp4",
513	            Container::M4a => "m4a",
514	            Container::Wav => "wav",
515	            Container::Aiff => "aiff",
516	            Container::Gif => "gif",
517	            Container::Apng => "apng",
518	            Container::Webm => "webm",
519	        }
520	    }
521	
522	    /// The output file's UTI. On the AVFoundation path Swift passes this
523	    /// straight to `outputFileType`, whose raw values ARE UTIs; on the
524	    /// ImageIO path it is the destination type
525	    /// `CGImageDestinationCreateWithURL` takes. Either way it is what the
526	    /// save panel's content type and file extension are derived from, which
527	    /// is why the two image formats name a real UTI here rather than
528	    /// nothing — an export that could not tell the panel it writes a `.gif`
529	    /// would be worse off than one whose type string a session would
530	    /// reject, and a session is never built for them.
531	    ///
532	    /// An APNG is written to an ordinary PNG destination — the animation
533	    /// lives in `acTL`/`fcTL` chunks inside a file that is still a PNG — so
534	    /// its type identifier is PNG's, not one of its own.
535	    ///
536	    /// The two LPCM rows' identifiers are exactly `AVFileType.wav` and
537	    /// `AVFileType.aiff`'s raw values, which is what lets
538	    /// `Exporter.fileType(for:)` resolve them from this string alone
539	    /// rather than growing a container list of its own.
540	    pub(crate) fn file_type(self) -> &'static str {
541	        match self {
542	            Container::Mov => "com.apple.quicktime-movie",
543	            Container::Mp4 => "public.mpeg-4",
544	            Container::M4a => "com.apple.m4a-audio",
545	            Container::Wav => "com.microsoft.waveform-audio",
546	            Container::Aiff => "public.aiff-audio",
547	            Container::Gif => "com.compuserve.gif",
548	            Container::Apng => "public.png",
549	            Container::Webm => "org.webmproject.webm",
550	        }
551	    }
552	
553	    /// Whether `shouldOptimizeForNetworkUse` defaults on. MP4 and M4A are
554	    /// the delivery containers people upload, and a leading `moov` atom
555	    /// lets a player start before the file is fully fetched. A ProRes MOV
556	    /// is an editing master handed to another application, where the
557	    /// rewrite pass buys nothing. An HEVC-with-alpha MOV is a delivery file
558	    /// too, and its default stays off all the same: that was the owner's
559	    /// choice for the row (spec §11 G-33), and the override turns it on. GIF
560	    /// and APNG have no `moov` atom and nothing to move: a viewer already
561	    /// starts on the first frame, and
562	    /// neither do WAV and AIFF — a RIFF or an IFF file is a header
563	    /// followed by samples, with no index to relocate, so the flag would
564	    /// be a request the writer has nothing to do about. A WebM's index (its
565	    /// SeekHead) is already at the front, so the flag is off and inert there
566	    /// too (spec §11 CX-15 (1)).
567	    pub(crate) fn optimizes_for_network(self) -> bool {
568	        matches!(self, Container::Mp4 | Container::M4a)
569	    }
570	
571	    /// Whether the container can hold sound. Every movie container can,
572	    /// and M4A, WAV and AIFF are nothing else; GIF and APNG are picture
573	    /// formats with no audio track in the file format at all, so
574	    /// `audio: false` for those is a fact about the container rather than
575	    /// a decision about the project.
576	    pub(crate) fn carries_audio(self) -> bool {

648	//! How an export override is READ and REFUSED — the vocabulary the export
649	//! settings resolve from, where `export_table.rs` is the table and
650	//! `export.rs` the resolution.
651	//!
652	//! Cut out of `export.rs` in road map 2's phase 5, and cut HERE for the
653	//! reason `props_check.rs` was cut out of `edit_props.rs`: a rule about
654	//! how a value is spelled and what makes it a refusal is a fact about the
655	//! VOCABULARY, not about the resolution. Nothing in this file knows which
656	//! preset asked, what the canvas is, or what the settings object ends up
657	//! looking like; everything in it answers one question — "is this JSON
658	//! value a legal `width` / `fps` / `range` / bitrate / decibel figure, and
659	//! if not, what do we tell the caller it was?".
660	//!
661	//! The cut also paid the size rule's toll. `export.rs` stood at 578 lines
662	//! against the ~600 soft cap and phase 5 added two containers, two preset
663	//! rows, a decibel validator, two override reads and two echo lines; a
664	//! file at the line gives something up before it takes anything on.
665	//!
666	//! Three rules hold for every reader here, and every new one must keep
667	//! them, because the sheet, the `export` tool and the test suite all lean
668	//! on them:
669	//!
670	//! 1. **Absent and explicit null are the same thing** — "use the preset".
671	//!    That is what lets the export sheet build one overrides object and
672	//!    null the fields whose control is greyed out.
673	//! 2. **An unknown key is ignored, silently.** A newer UI may send fields
674	//!    this build has never heard of and must still get an export.
675	//! 3. **A refusal names the offending value**, through [`describe`], and
676	//!    the message is lowercase and starts `export <key> must be …`. The
677	//!    key is in the message because a caller sending six overrides needs
678	//!    to know which one it was.
679	//!
680	//! [`describe`] itself is not about export at all any more: five modules
681	//! outside this one (`edit.rs`, `edit_props.rs`, `edit_action.rs`,
682	//! `edit_paste.rs`, `edit_track.rs`) name it `crate::export::describe` for
683	//! their own error messages, so `export.rs` re-exports it under that path
684	//! and the cut costs those files nothing. [`spelled`] sits beside it for
685	//! the same reason: a vocabulary value's own JSON spelling, for a sentence
686	//! (`lut.rs`, `media_color.rs`, `edit_relink.rs`).
687	
688	use serde_json::Value;
689	
690	use crate::dynamic_range::DynamicRange;
691	use crate::export_table::EncoderSpeed;

696	/// A JSON value as short text for an error message, truncated on a char
697	/// boundary so a pasted megabyte of JSON cannot become the error string.
698	pub(crate) fn describe(value: &Value) -> String {
699	    let text = value.to_string();
700	    if text.chars().count() <= 40 {
701	        text
702	    } else {
703	        format!("{} …", text.chars().take(40).collect::<String>())
704	    }
705	}

707	/// A vocabulary value's JSON spelling (`warm`, `video`), serde's own, so a
708	/// sentence names it as the file and the schema do.
709	pub(crate) fn spelled<T: serde::Serialize>(value: T) -> String {
710	    serde_json::to_value(value)
711	        .ok()
712	        .and_then(|value| value.as_str().map(str::to_string))
713	        .unwrap_or_default()
714	}

716	/// The overrides object itself: `None` for absent, null or an empty
717	/// request, `Some` for an object, and an `Err` naming the value for
718	/// anything else. One place, so "overrides must be a json object" is the
719	/// same sentence however the caller got here.
720	pub(crate) fn object(overrides: Option<&Value>) -> Result<Option<&Value>, String> {
721	    match overrides {
722	        None => Ok(None),
723	        Some(Value::Null) => Ok(None),
724	        Some(value) if value.is_object() => Ok(Some(value)),
725	        Some(value) => Err(format!(
726	            "export overrides must be a json object, not {}",
727	            describe(value)
728	        )),
729	    }
730	}

732	/// An override field, or `None` when absent or explicitly null (null means
733	/// "use the preset", so a caller can build one overrides object and leave
734	/// the fields it does not care about).
735	fn field<'a>(overrides: Option<&'a Value>, key: &str) -> Option<&'a Value> {
736	    overrides.and_then(|o| o.get(key)).filter(|v| !v.is_null())
737	}

741	/// A strictly positive integer override — the pixel dimensions and the two
742	/// bitrates, which want the identical check. `u64::MAX` is not the ceiling
743	/// on purpose: a bitrate is bits per second, and `u32`'s 4.3 Gbit/s is an
744	/// order of magnitude past anything deliverable (ProRes 422 at 4K is about
745	/// 0.7), so the same bound that keeps a width sane keeps a bitrate honest.
746	/// Zero and negative both land in the error arm, which names the value.
747	pub(crate) fn positive_u32(overrides: Option<&Value>, key: &str) -> Result<Option<u32>, String> {
748	    let Some(value) = field(overrides, key) else {
749	        return Ok(None);
750	    };
751	    match value.as_u64() {
752	        Some(n) if n > 0 && n <= u64::from(u32::MAX) => Ok(Some(n as u32)),
753	        _ => Err(format!(
754	            "export {key} must be a positive integer, not {}",
755	            describe(value)
756	        )),
757	    }
758	}

760	/// A decibel override: a finite number inside `[min, max]`. The f64 twin
761	/// of [`positive_u32`], and a separate function because the two loudness
762	/// figures are NEGATIVE FRACTIONS — −14.5 LUFS is a real request — so
763	/// every guard `positive_u32` applies is the wrong one here.
764	///
765	/// `as_f64` is the whole type check: `serde_json` answers `None` for a
766	/// bool, a string, an array and an object alike, so the error arm catches
767	/// them all and names what arrived. Non-finite is checked even though JSON
768	/// cannot spell a NaN or an infinity — the function takes a `Value` from
769	/// whoever has one, and a bound comparison against a NaN is silently false
770	/// rather than an error.
771	fn decibels(
772	    overrides: Option<&Value>,
773	    key: &str,
774	    min: f64,
775	    max: f64,
776	) -> Result<Option<f64>, String> {
777	    let Some(value) = field(overrides, key) else {
778	        return Ok(None);
779	    };
780	    match value.as_f64() {
781	        Some(db) if db.is_finite() && db >= min && db <= max => Ok(Some(db)),
782	        _ => Err(format!(
783	            "export {key} must be a number from {min} to {max}, not {}",
784	            describe(value)
785	        )),
786	    }
787	}
788	
789	/// The bottom of the loudness target's range. −70 LUFS is BS.1770-4's own
790	/// absolute gate: a programme quieter than that measures as nothing at
791	/// all, so a target at or below it is a request the measurement cannot
792	/// even express. The top is 0 LUFS — full scale, unwise but legal, and the
793	/// bound is where it is so the message is about the value.
794	const LOUDNESS_MIN: f64 = -70.0;
795	const LOUDNESS_MAX: f64 = 0.0;
796	
797	/// The true-peak ceiling's range. 0 dBTP is legal (and what a master with
798	/// no headroom asks for); −20 is far below anything a deliverable wants
799	/// and exists only so a mistyped LUFS figure lands in the error arm rather
800	/// than turning the programme down by 60 dB.
801	const PEAK_MIN: f64 = -20.0;
802	const PEAK_MAX: f64 = 0.0;
803	
804	/// The two loudness overrides, read together: `loudness_lufs`, the
805	/// integrated target the export is normalised to, and `peak_dbtp`, the
806	/// true-peak ceiling of the export's master limiter.
807	///
808	/// **Either may come alone** (spec §11 AU-27). Every export with sound runs
809	/// through a master limiter at `peak_dbtp`, −1 dBTP when it is not asked
810	/// for, so a ceiling on its own is not inert: it is the limiter's ceiling,
811	/// with or without a target, and is accepted and echoed as every other
812	/// override is.
813	///
814	/// Both are emitted by the resolver only when asked for, exactly as the
815	/// bitrates are: an absent `loudness_lufs` is "do not normalise", which is
816	/// what `ExportSettings.loudnessLufs == nil` says on the Swift side, and an
817	/// absent `peak_dbtp` is the master's default ceiling there.
818	pub(crate) fn loudness(overrides: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(Option<f64>, Option<f64>), String> {
819	    let target = decibels(overrides, "loudness_lufs", LOUDNESS_MIN, LOUDNESS_MAX)?;
820	    let ceiling = decibels(overrides, "peak_dbtp", PEAK_MIN, PEAK_MAX)?;
821	    Ok((target, ceiling))
822	}

917	/// The `fps` override as `[num, den]`, or `default` when it is absent.
918	/// Both terms are read as `u64` and bounded by `u32::MAX` because that is
919	/// what [`Fps`] holds, and both must be non-zero: a zero numerator is a
920	/// frozen export and a zero denominator is a division by nothing, and
921	/// either would reach the frame-snapping arithmetic before anyone noticed.
922	pub(crate) fn fps(overrides: Option<&Value>, default: Fps) -> Result<Fps, String> {
923	    let Some(value) = field(overrides, "fps") else {
924	        return Ok(default);
925	    };
926	    let terms = value.as_array().and_then(|a| {
927	        match (
928	            a.first().and_then(Value::as_u64),
929	            a.get(1).and_then(Value::as_u64),
930	        ) {
931	            (Some(num), Some(den)) if a.len() == 2 => Some((num, den)),
932	            _ => None,
933	        }
934	    });
935	    match terms {
936	        Some((num, den))
937	            if num > 0 && den > 0 && num <= u64::from(u32::MAX) && den <= u64::from(u32::MAX) =>
938	        {
939	            Ok(Fps {
940	                num: num as u32,
941	                den: den as u32,
942	            })
943	        }
944	        _ => Err(format!(
945	            "export fps must be [num, den] with non-zero terms, not {}",
946	            describe(value)
947	        )),
948	    }
949	}

961	/// The `range` override as the raw `(start, duration)` pair it asked for,
962	/// each falling back to its half of `default` — which is `(0, the whole
963	/// project)`, so `{"start": …}` alone keeps the project's length and
964	/// `{"duration": …}` alone keeps its start.
965	///
966	/// RAW is the word: nothing here snaps or clamps. Both are decisions about
967	/// a project and an export rate, which this file knows nothing about, and
968	/// the ORDER of the two (snap first, then clamp) is load-bearing enough to
969	/// stay visible where the settings are resolved.
970	pub(crate) fn range(
971	    overrides: Option<&Value>,
972	    default: (Ticks, Ticks),
973	) -> Result<(Ticks, Ticks), String> {
974	    let Some(range) = field(overrides, "range") else {
975	        return Ok(default);
976	    };
977	    if !range.is_object() {
978	        return Err(format!(
979	            "export range must be a json object with start and duration, not {}",
980	            describe(range)
981	        ));
982	    }
983	    let (mut start, mut duration) = default;
984	    if let Some(value) = field(Some(range), "start") {
985	        start = ticks(value, "range start")?;
986	    }
987	    if let Some(value) = field(Some(range), "duration") {
988	        duration = ticks(value, "range duration")?;
989	    }
990	    Ok((start, duration))
991	}

168	    /// `peak_dbtp` convert to `loudnessLufs` and `peakDbtp` on their own.

170	    /// a `CodingKeys` enum is exhaustive, and a case left out is a field

177	    /// `video`.** Nothing decodes them, so adding cases would add two stored

181	    /// only one here. A future reader of `audio` or `video` adds the case —
182	    /// it does not infer the answer from this list's silence.

184	        case preset, container, codec, width, height, fps, range
185	        case avPreset = "avfPreset"
186	        case fileType, optimizeForNetwork, videoBitrate, audioBitrate
187	        case loudnessLufs, peakDbtp, alpha, color, writer, encoderSpeed, audioBits, stems
188	    }

190	    private enum RangeKeys: String, CodingKey {
191	        case start, duration
192	    }

194	    init(from decoder: Decoder) throws {
195	        let c = try decoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
196	        preset = c.lenient(.preset, "")
197	        container = c.lenient(.container, "mov")
198	        codec = c.lenient(.codec, "h264")
199	        width = c.lenient(.width, 1920)
200	        height = c.lenient(.height, 1080)
201	        fps = c.lenient(.fps, Fps.thirty)
202	        let range = try? c.nestedContainer(keyedBy: RangeKeys.self, forKey: .range)
203	        start = range?.lenient(.start, 0) ?? 0
204	        duration = range?.lenient(.duration, 0) ?? 0
205	        avPreset = c.lenient(.avPreset)
206	        fileType = c.lenient(.fileType)
207	        optimizeForNetwork = c.lenient(.optimizeForNetwork, true)
208	        videoBitrate = c.lenient(.videoBitrate)
209	        audioBitrate = c.lenient(.audioBitrate)
210	        loudnessLufs = c.lenient(.loudnessLufs)
211	        peakDbtp = c.lenient(.peakDbtp)
212	        // False is the safe default: only `prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha`,
213	        // `vp9_alpha_webm` and `apng` answer true, and a core that predates phase 7 does not emit
214	        // the key at all. Its silence UNDER-reports — that core has no
215	        // `prores_4444` row to describe, but its `apng` row wrote alpha then as it does
216	        // now — and under-reporting is the direction that cannot hurt: this
217	        // key only ADDS the footnote's "alpha" and ARMS
218	        // `ExportWriter.checkAlphaSurvivesTheSize`, so false promises less
219	        // than the file holds where true would promise more.
220	        alpha = c.lenient(.alpha, false)
221	        color = c.lenient(.color)
222	        writer = c.lenient(.writer)
223	        let speed: String? = c.lenient(.encoderSpeed)
224	        encoderSpeed = speed.flatMap(EncoderSpeed.init(rawValue:))
225	        audioBits = c.lenient(.audioBits)
226	        stems = c.lenient(.stems, [])
227	    }

229	    var renderSize: CGSize { CGSize(width: width, height: height) }

     4	/// The export card's two commits, Export… and Add to Queue, which end in a save panel and hand
     5	/// the resolved settings to the editor: `commit(queue:)` with the three button actions that
     6	/// reach it, `recipeOptions`, `suggestedName` and `panelMessage`. An extension of
     7	/// `ExportSheetController` in a file of its own, a pure move out of the controller before the
     8	/// HDR road map's export range (hdr H-0).
     9	extension ExportSheetController {
    10	    // MARK: - Commit
    11	
    12	    @objc func cancelClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
    13	        dismiss(self)
    14	    }
    15	
    16	    /// Export… — write it now, behind a progress sheet.
    17	    @objc func exportClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
    18	        commit(queue: false)
    19	    }
    20	
    21	    /// Add to Queue — write it later, behind nothing. The SAME commit, in one
    22	    /// method, so the buttons cannot drift (road map 2's phase 7e).
    23	    @objc func queueClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
    24	        commit(queue: true)
    25	    }
    26	
    27	    /// Hands off to the save panel, then to `EditorViewController`'s
    28	    /// `beginExport` — or, for Add to Queue, its `enqueueExport`. The settings
    29	    /// are captured BEFORE the dismissal: after it this controller's window is
    30	    /// gone and its controls are on their way out of the view tree. Everything
    31	    /// above the handoff is the same for both buttons and is written once for
    32	    /// that reason: a queued job is not a second kind of export, it is this
    33	    /// one held until its turn.
    34	    private func commit(queue: Bool) {
    35	        // End any edit in a Custom field first. A mouse click on a button
    36	        // does not take the first responder from a text field, so the value
    37	        // typed there has not been committed — `controlTextDidEndEditing`,
    38	        // and the resolve it runs, fire only when the field editor resigns —
    39	        // and `resolved` still describes the size from BEFORE the edit.
    40	        // Handing the first responder to nobody makes it resign now,
    41	        // synchronously, so the read below sees the numbers on screen. A
    42	        // field whose text its formatter rejects refuses to resign; that is
    43	        // the person's to fix, so the click just beeps.
    44	        guard endSheetFieldEditing() else { return }
    45	        guard let editor = editor, let settings = resolved,
    46	              let window = editor.view.window
    47	        else {
    48	            NSSound.beep()
    49	            return
    50	        }
    51	        // Read while the controls still exist. `recipeOptions` is not part of
    52	        // `settings` and never can be: the burn-in changes the PICTURE, so it
    53	        // travels with the description of the picture rather than through the
    54	        // override table, which drops a key it does not know without a word
    55	        // (`RecipeOptions`).
    56	        let options = recipeOptions
    57	        // Remembered on the COMMIT and not on the dismissal: a card somebody
    58	        // opened, fiddled with and cancelled is not a choice they made — and
    59	        // queueing a job is as much a choice as exporting one, so both
    60	        // buttons record it.
    61	        currentChoice.remember()
    62	        let name = suggestedName(for: settings, in: editor)
    63	        dismiss(self)
    64	
    65	        let panel = NSSavePanel()
    66	        panel.nameFieldStringValue = name
    67	        panel.canCreateDirectories = true
    68	        panel.isExtensionHidden = false
    69	        panel.message = Self.panelMessage(for: settings)
    70	        if let type = Exporter.contentType(for: settings) {
    71	            panel.allowedContentTypes = [type]
    72	        }
    73	        // AppKit queues this behind the sheet that is on its way out, so the
    74	        // panel appears once the settings card has finished leaving.
    75	        panel.beginSheetModal(for: window) { [weak editor] response in
    76	            guard response == .OK, let url = panel.url, let editor = editor else { return }
    77	            // The handoff, and the only place the two buttons differ. The
    78	            // project and its media are read on the far side of it, at the
    79	            // moment the destination is known — which for a queued job is the
    80	            // whole of what makes it immutable (`ExportQueueController`).
    81	            if queue {
    82	                editor.enqueueExport(settings: settings, to: url, options: options)
    83	            } else {
    84	                editor.beginExport(settings: settings, to: url, options: options)
    85	            }
    86	        }
    87	    }
    88	
    89	    /// What the card asks of the RECIPE rather than of the export settings —
    90	    /// today, the burn-in and nothing else.
    91	    var recipeOptions: RecipeOptions {
    92	        RecipeOptions(burnInTimecode: burnInCheckbox.state == .on)
    93	    }
    94	
    95	    /// The document's name with the container's extension: `displayStem`, the
    96	    /// title with the package's own extension off and NOTHING else off, so
    97	    /// "Board v1.2" is `Board v1.2.mp4` (`ProjectDocument+DisplayStem.swift`).
    98	    private func suggestedName(for settings: ExportSettings, in editor: EditorViewController)
    99	        -> String
   100	    {
   101	        let stem = editor.document?.displayStem ?? ProjectDocument.untitledDisplayName
   102	        return stem + "." + Exporter.fileExtension(for: settings)
   103	    }
   104	
   105	    /// The save panel's one line about what is being written. "As a movie"
   106	    /// was wrong for half the table: a GIF or an APNG is an animated image
   107	    /// and the audio-only row writes no picture at all. The classes are the
   108	    /// sheet's own (`Applies`, `isFrameSequence`), so a format that is
   109	    /// neither is a movie by the same reading that gave it a Size popup.
   110	    private static func panelMessage(for settings: ExportSettings) -> String {
   111	        if settings.isAudioOnly { return "Export the timeline's audio." }
   112	        if isFrameSequence(container: settings.container) {
   113	            return "Export the timeline as an animated \(settings.container.uppercased())."
   114	        }
   115	        return "Export the timeline as a movie."
   116	    }
   117	}
