259	    /// liked, so the sheet's "1920 × 1080" was a wish. Here the encoder is
260	    /// told the size the sheet promised, and the scaling mode is one of two
261	    /// (spec §11 G-33 (c)). A frame of the canvas's exact shape, or one more
262	    /// than a pixel off it, gets `AVVideoScalingModeResizeAspect`: the canvas
263	    /// fitted inside, letterboxed rather than distorted when the two shapes
264	    /// differ. A frame WITHIN a pixel of the canvas's shape (`fillsTheBox`)
265	    /// gets `AVVideoScalingModeResizeAspectFill`: the picture covers the
266	    /// frame, where a fit wrote one or two black lines along an edge — the
267	    /// evened Document row on a canvas with an odd edge, an odd size typed
268	    /// in the canvas's proportions, and a standard row whose long edge
269	    /// rounded. The frame itself is `encodedSize`'s answer,
270	    /// because `checkAlphaSurvivesTheSize` and `fillsTheBox` have to compare
271	    /// against the same number.
272	    ///
273	    /// **HEVC with alpha** is the HEVC row's dictionary — the bit rate, the
274	    /// key-frame interval, the expected frame rate — plus the one key that
275	    /// says what the pixels handed to the encoder ARE: straight, because the
276	    /// video pump un-premultiplies an alpha row's frames first
277	    /// (`ExportStraightAlpha`, spec §11 G-35 (e), amending G-33 (d)). There
278	    /// is no alpha-quality key and no profile key (G-33 (d) has what was
279	    /// measured with and without).
280	    ///
281	    /// **Bitrate.** `settings.videoBitrate` when the core resolved one. When
282	    /// it did not, a rate computed from the frame — bits per pixel per frame,
283	    /// halved for HEVC — rather than none at all: with no
284	    /// `AVVideoAverageBitRateKey` VideoToolbox picks a conservative default
285	    /// that visibly under-runs a 4K timeline. ProRes gets neither: its rate
286	    /// is a property of the profile.
287	    static func videoSettings(
288	        _ settings: ExportSettings, canvas: CGSize
289	    ) throws -> [String: Any] {
290	        guard let codec = codecType(for: settings.codec) else {
291	            throw Exporter.ExportError.presetUnavailable(presetName(settings))
292	        }
293	        let frame = encodedSize(settings)
294	        let fills = fillsTheBox(settings, canvas: canvas)
295	        var output: [String: Any] = [
296	            AVVideoCodecKey: codec,
297	            AVVideoWidthKey: frame.width,
298	            AVVideoHeightKey: frame.height,
299	            AVVideoScalingModeKey: fills
300	                ? AVVideoScalingModeResizeAspectFill : AVVideoScalingModeResizeAspect,
301	            // The compositor works in SDR 709 and converts HDR sources itself
302	            // at step 0 (GR-15, §7.5), so tagging the output 709 is a
303	            // statement of what the pixels ARE, not a conversion.
304	            AVVideoColorPropertiesKey: [
305	                AVVideoColorPrimariesKey: AVVideoColorPrimaries_ITU_R_709_2,
306	                AVVideoTransferFunctionKey: AVVideoTransferFunction_ITU_R_709_2,
307	                AVVideoYCbCrMatrixKey: AVVideoYCbCrMatrix_ITU_R_709_2,
308	            ],
309	        ]
310	        // An HLG project's 10-bit row (spec §11 HD-13 (j), HD-14 (c), the
311	        // core's `color`): its pixels are HLG or PQ over BT.2020, and so are
312	        // its tags; its SDR version (`sdr`) keeps the BT.709 tags above.
313	        let hlg = settings.color == "hlg"
314	        let pq = settings.color == "pq"
315	        if hlg || pq {
316	            output[AVVideoColorPropertiesKey] = [
317	                AVVideoColorPrimariesKey: AVVideoColorPrimaries_ITU_R_2020,
318	                AVVideoTransferFunctionKey: pq
319	                    ? REDACTED : REDACTED,
320	                AVVideoYCbCrMatrixKey: AVVideoYCbCrMatrix_ITU_R_2020,
321	            ]
322	        }
323	        // HDR10's fixed metadata (spec §11 HD-5, HD-14 (d)): ProRes takes the
324	        // two keys as a compression dictionary of their own (measured, M7).
325	        if pq, codec == .proRes422 || codec == .proRes4444 {
326	            output[AVVideoCompressionPropertiesKey] = hdr10Metadata
327	        }
328	        guard codec != .proRes422, codec != .proRes4444 else { return output }
329	
330	        var compression: [String: Any] = [
331	            AVVideoAverageBitRateKey: settings.videoBitrate.map { max(1, $0) }
332	                ?? defaultVideoBitrate(settings, codec: codec),
333	            // A keyframe at least every two seconds. Deliberate, not a
334	            // default: an exported movie is scrubbed and re-cut, and
335	            // VideoToolbox's own interval is long enough to make that
336	            // painful.
337	            AVVideoMaxKeyFrameIntervalDurationKey: 2.0,
338	        ]
339	        if settings.fps.double > 0 {
340	            compression[AVVideoExpectedSourceFrameRateKey] = Int(settings.fps.double.rounded())
341	        }
342	        if codec == .h264 {
343	            compression[AVVideoProfileLevelKey] = AVVideoProfileLevelH264HighAutoLevel
344	        }
345	        // Pinned to 8-bit Main (spec §11 PR-3): given no profile, VideoToolbox
346	        // follows its input's format, and the compositor's 16-bit frames
347	        // gave Main 10. `frameForm` rounds this row's frame to 8 bits as
348	        // well; the pin is what holds Main if a deep frame ever reaches it.
349	        // `hevc_10bit` is the same codec pinned to Main 10, fed deep frames.
350	        if codec == .hevc, isMain10(settings) {
351	            compression[AVVideoProfileLevelKey] = kVTProfileLevel_HEVC_Main10_AutoLevel as String
352	        } else if codec == .hevc {
353	            compression[AVVideoProfileLevelKey] = kVTProfileLevel_HEVC_Main_AutoLevel as String
354	        }
355	        if codec == .hevcWithAlpha {
356	            compression[kVTCompressionPropertyKey_AlphaChannelMode as String] =
357	                kVTAlphaChannelMode_StraightAlpha
358	        }
359	        // Dolby Vision off (spec §11 HD-5, choice 5a): without the key
360	        // VideoToolbox adds a profile 8.4 configuration and RPU frames to an
361	        // HLG HEVC Main 10 file by itself (the brief's M7).
362	        if hlg, codec == .hevc {
363	            compression[kVTCompressionPropertyKey_HDRMetadataInsertionMode as String] =
364	                kVTHDRMetadataInsertionMode_None
365	        }
366	        // HDR10's metadata beside the other keys, with NO insertion-mode key:
367	        // explicit values are written exactly and no Dolby Vision is added
368	        // (spec §11 HD-14 (f), measured).
369	        if pq, codec == .hevc {
370	            compression.merge(hdr10Metadata) { _, metadata in metadata }
371	        }
372	        output[AVVideoCompressionPropertiesKey] = compression
373	        return output
374	    }
375	
376	    /// HDR10's mastering display and content light level as VideoToolbox's
377	    /// two compression keys (`OutputTransform`'s blobs, spec §11 HD-14 (d)).
378	    static var hdr10Metadata: [String: Any] {
379	        [
380	            kVTCompressionPropertyKey_MasteringDisplayColorVolume as String:
381	                OutputTransform.masteringDisplay,
382	            kVTCompressionPropertyKey_ContentLightLevelInfo as String:
383	                OutputTransform.contentLightLevel,
384	        ]
385	    }
386	
387	    /// What the video pump makes of each 64RGBAHalf frame before the encoder
388	    /// (spec §11 PR-3, `ExportFrames`): `hevc_alpha`'s rounded to 8 bits and
389	    /// straightened, any other alpha row's (`prores_4444`) straightened in
390	    /// float, `h264`'s and `hevc`'s rounded to 8 bits; nil hands the frame on
391	    /// as drawn. The two 8-bit codecs encode a ramp worse from half-float
392	    /// frames: H.264 8.80 steps RMS against 6.27 from 32BGRA, and `hevc`
393	    /// (Main) 9.04 against 6.46 (precision PR1). `hevc_10bit` maps to `.hevc`
394	    /// too, so it is asked by its codec NAME first: Main 10 takes the deep
395	    /// frames, which is the row's whole point.
396	    static func frameForm(_ settings: ExportSettings) -> ExportFrameForm? {
397	        let codec = codecType(for: settings.codec)
398	        if settings.alpha { return codec == .hevcWithAlpha ? .straightEightBit : .straightHalf }
399	        if isMain10(settings) { return nil }
400	        return codec == .h264 || codec == .hevc ? .eightBit : nil
401	    }
402	
403	    /// Whether the row is `hevc_10bit` (spec §11 PR-3): `.hevc` with the
404	    /// Main 10 profile and the compositor's frames as drawn. Asked by the
405	    /// codec name because `codecType(for:)` answers `.hevc` for both HEVC rows.
406	    private static func isMain10(_ settings: ExportSettings) -> Bool {
407	        settings.codec.lowercased() == "hevc_10bit"
408	    }
409	
410	    /// The core's codec name as an `AVVideoCodecType`. nil is a refusal, not
411	    /// a fallback: writing H.264 because "vp9" was not understood would put a
412	    /// file on disk that is not the one asked for.
413	    private static func codecType(for codec: String) -> AVVideoCodecType? {
414	        switch codec.lowercased() {
415	        case "h264", "avc", "avc1": return .h264
416	        case "hevc", "h265", "hvc1": return .hevc
417	        case "hevc_alpha": return .hevcWithAlpha
418	        case "hevc_10bit": return .hevc
419	        case "prores_422", "prores", "prores422": return .proRes422
420	        case "prores_4444", "prores4444": return .proRes4444
421	        default: return nil
422	        }
423	    }
424	
425	    /// What to call the settings in a refusal: the core's preset id when it
426	    /// gave one, else the codec that could not be written.
427	    static func presetName(_ settings: ExportSettings) -> String {
428	        settings.preset.isEmpty ? settings.codec : settings.preset
429	    }
430	
431	    /// Bits per second for a frame of this size at this rate. The constants
432	    /// are the usual delivery figures — about 9 Mbps for 1080p30 H.264 and
433	    /// half that for HEVC, with or without alpha — clamped so a tiny canvas
434	    /// still gets a usable rate and a huge one cannot ask for a file no disk
435	    /// wants.
436	    private static func defaultVideoBitrate(
437	        _ settings: ExportSettings, codec: AVVideoCodecType
438	    ) -> Int {
439	        let perPixel = (codec == .hevc || codec == .hevcWithAlpha) ? 0.07 : 0.14
440	        return defaultVideoBitrate(settings, bitsPerPixel: perPixel)
441	    }
442	
443	    /// The same rate at `bitsPerPixel` per frame — the AV1 row's "Format
444	    /// default" is HEVC's 0.07 (spec §11 CX-9 (2)).
445	    static func defaultVideoBitrate(_ settings: ExportSettings, bitsPerPixel: Double) -> Int {
446	        let pixels = Double(max(1, settings.width)) * Double(max(1, settings.height))
447	        let rate = settings.fps.double > 0 ? settings.fps.double : 30
448	        return Int(min(max(pixels * rate * bitsPerPixel, 1_000_000), 200_000_000))
449	    }
450	
451	    /// Even, and never zero — H.264 and HEVC macroblocks come in pairs.
452	    /// `encodedSize` is the only caller and says which rows want it.
453	    private static func evenDimension(_ value: Int) -> Int {
454	        let clamped = max(2, value)
455	        return clamped - (clamped % 2)
456	    }
457	
458	    /// The shape of the master's 16-bit output (`ExportAudioMaster`, spec §11
459	    /// AU-27): 48 kHz, 2 channels, 16-bit interleaved little-endian LPCM. The
460	    /// same format the ProRes path writes, and the one AAC, Opus and ProRes
461	    /// are fed. Nothing reads the mix in it any more: every export reads the
462	    /// float mix and the master quantises it once, after the gain and the
463	    /// limiter (#86). A 24-bit WAV or AIFF is the same shape at 24 bits
464	    /// (`audioSettings`, AU-29).
465	    static let decodedAudioSettings: [String: Any] = [
466	        AVFormatIDKey: Int(kAudioFormatLinearPCM),
467	        AVSampleRateKey: 48000,
468	        AVNumberOfChannelsKey: 2,
469	        AVLinearPCMBitDepthKey: 16,
470	        AVLinearPCMIsFloatKey: false,
471	        AVLinearPCMIsBigEndianKey: false,
472	        AVLinearPCMIsNonInterleaved: false,
473	    ]
474	
475	    /// The encoder settings for the sound: LPCM where the row asks for it, so
476	    /// a master stays a master, and AAC everywhere else. `settings.audioBitrate`
477	    /// when the core resolved one, else 192 kbps — stereo AAC's
478	    /// transparent-enough rate and what the M1 presets landed on.
479	    ///
480	    /// **Two codecs mean LPCM (`ExportSettings.carriesLinearPCM(codec:)`), and
481	    /// the CONTAINER decides the byte order.** ProRes has since M2 (§7.8
482	    /// pairs the profile with uncompressed sound), and phase 5's `audio_wav`
483	    /// / `audio_aiff` rows carry the codec `lpcm` outright. The dictionary handed to the encoder is then literally
484	    /// `decodedAudioSettings` — at 24 bits when `settings.audioBits` asks
485	    /// (spec §11 AU-29) — so nothing is converted on the way:
486	    /// `ExportAudioMaster` produces that shape from the float read. The exception is
487	    /// AIFF, which is big-endian by definition where WAV and QuickTime are
488	    /// little. Getting that flag wrong is not a subtle bug, and it was measured rather than
489	    /// reasoned about: on macOS 26.5.1 `AVAssetWriter.canAdd` answers FALSE
490	    /// for AAC settings into a `.wav` and FALSE for a little-endian LPCM
491	    /// dictionary into an `.aiff`, so either mistake reaches the user as
492	    /// `.presetUnavailable` for a format the table advertises. With the
493	    /// branch as written, one twenty-second tone came out of both rows the
494	    /// same size and decoded to identical PCM, sample for sample.
495	    ///
496	    /// A row whose codec is `lpcm` in a container this build has no rule for
497	    /// still gets little-endian LPCM rather than AAC, because AAC in an
498	    /// uncompressed container is the failure that reads as
499	    /// `.presetUnavailable` and sends the reader looking at the preset table.
500	    static func audioSettings(_ settings: ExportSettings) -> [String: Any] {
501	        guard ExportSettings.carriesLinearPCM(codec: settings.codec) else {
502	            return [
503	                AVFormatIDKey: Int(kAudioFormatMPEG4AAC),
504	                AVSampleRateKey: 48000,
505	                AVNumberOfChannelsKey: 2,
506	                AVEncoderBitRateKey: settings.audioBitrate.map { max(1, $0) } ?? 192_000,
507	            ]
508	        }
509	        var lpcm = decodedAudioSettings
510	        if settings.audioBits == 24 { lpcm[AVLinearPCMBitDepthKey] = 24 }
511	        if settings.container.lowercased() == "aiff" { lpcm[AVLinearPCMIsBigEndianKey] = true }
512	        return lpcm
513	    }
514	
515	    /// Whether this container can hold a chapter track (see `addChapters`).
516	    /// The QuickTime family and nothing else: a chapter list is a text track
517	    /// associated with the movie's own, and WAV, AIFF and the two image
518	    /// formats have no track to associate it with.
519	    static func carriesChapters(_ settings: ExportSettings) -> Bool {
520	        switch settings.container.lowercased() {
521	        case "mov", "quicktime", "mp4", "m4v", "m4a": return true
522	        default: return false
523	        }
524	    }
525	}

3	/// The export sheet's ANSWER half: read the controls, ask the core what they
4	/// describe, and repaint the card from what it said.
5	///
6	/// The seam is the §7 rule the sheet is built on, drawn as a file boundary.
7	/// `ExportSheetController.swift` owns the controls — it makes the popups and
8	/// the fields, lists the sizes, and hands a person something to choose with.
9	/// Nothing there decides an output size, a rate or a duration, because
10	/// nothing in this dialog does: every number the card shows comes back from
11	/// `rc_export_settings`, and this file is the whole of the round trip. It
12	/// turns a selection into the override object the core reads (`overrides()`),
13	/// sends it (`resolve()`), and writes the answer into the readout, the
14	/// footnote and the controls' enablement (`syncReadout()`). Between those
15	/// three, the `current…` accessors are the one place a popup index becomes a
16	/// meaning, so a control's index arithmetic is never spelled twice.
17	///
18	/// The one number the sheet DOES choose is the bit rate, and it is here for
19	/// that reason rather than beside the Quality popup: a tier is a REQUEST
20	/// (`ExportSheetOptions.swift` holds the ladder), and turning one into bits
21	/// per second needs the frame the controls are asking for — which is
22	/// `requestedFormat()`, three accessors deep into this file and nowhere near
23	/// the popup.
24	///
25	/// The cut is the size payment `ExportSheetController.swift` owed at 1114
26	/// lines against app/CLAUDE.md's ~600 cap, and it is a pure move: the same
27	/// methods, in the same order, with the same bodies. **The toll is
28	/// visibility**, for the reason `ExporterLoudness.swift` records — `private`
29	/// on an extension member reaches only its own file, and a stored property
30	/// cannot live in an extension at all. So every control, every field and
31	/// every piece of state this file reads is internal in the file that
32	/// declares it, and the four members the controls call back into —
33	/// `resolve()`, `currentPreset`, `isCustomSize` and `isCustomLoudness` — are
34	/// internal here. Everything else below stays `private`, because a `private`
35	/// extension member is reachable from the rest of THIS file, and nothing
36	/// outside it has ever asked.
37	/// Phase 7 added the OTHER direction to this file, and it belongs here for the
38	/// same reason the first one does: `currentChoice` is a reading of the
39	/// controls, exactly as `overrides()` is, and `apply(_:)` is that reading run
40	/// backwards. Keeping the pair together is what makes a saved preset and the
41	/// remembered choice provably the same thing as clicking each control by hand —
42	/// there is one account of what a stored choice means, and both halves of it
43	/// are on one screen.
44	extension ExportSheetController {
45	
46	    // MARK: - Resolving
47	
48	    /// Asks the core for the settings the current controls describe, then
49	    /// repaints the readout from the answer.
50	    ///
51	    /// A refusal is not an error dialog: the message goes in the readout and
52	    /// Export greys out, so a bad override reads as "this combination is not
53	    /// available" rather than interrupting the person adjusting it.
54	    func resolve() {
55	        guard let project = editor?.document?.project, let preset = currentPreset else {
56	            resolved = nil
57	            resolveError = "This build has no export presets."
58	            syncReadout()
59	            return
60	        }
61	        // A format whose sizes the core could not list is not exported at
62	        // all, whatever the settings call would answer: the one refusal
63	        // `rc_export_sizes` shares with `rc_export_settings` is an unknown
64	        // preset, but a listing can also fail on its own (a reply this
65	        // build cannot decode), and the size the sheet would then send is
66	        // the fields' clamped floor, 16 × 16, which nobody asked for.
67	        if let message = sizesError {
68	            resolved = nil
69	            resolveError = message
70	            syncReadout()
71	            return
72	        }
73	        // An empty Custom field is not a size. Its formatter accepts the
74	        // empty string as "no value", `integerValue` reads that as 0, and
75	        // the clamp would turn it into the 16-pixel floor — an export
76	        // nobody asked for, reached by clearing a field and clicking
77	        // Export…, since that click commits the field before it reads.
78	        if isCustomSize, currentApplies.size,
79	            widthField.stringValue.isEmpty || heightField.stringValue.isEmpty
80	        {
81	            resolved = nil
82	            resolveError = "Type a width and a height, or pick a size from the list."
83	            syncReadout()
84	            return
85	        }
86	        // The same rule for the Custom loudness field, and for the same
87	        // reason: an empty field is not a target, and reading it as one would
88	        // export at whatever the clamp's floor happens to be.
89	        if isCustomLoudness, currentApplies.loudness, loudnessField.stringValue.isEmpty {
90	            resolved = nil
91	            resolveError = "Type a loudness target in LUFS, or pick one from the list."
92	            syncReadout()
93	            return
94	        }
95	        do {
96	            resolved = try ReelExport.settings(
97	                project, preset: preset.id, overrides: overrides())
98	            resolveError = nil
99	        } catch {
100	            resolved = nil
101	            resolveError = error.localizedDescription
102	        }
103	        syncReadout()
104	    }
105	
106	    // MARK: - The card as a value
107	
108	    /// The controls as an `ExportChoice`, with the sheet's own gating applied:
109	    /// a control the chosen format cannot take (`Applies`) contributes
110	    /// nothing, exactly as it contributes no override. So a preset saved off
111	    /// an audio-only row carries no size, and one saved off a GIF carries no
112	    /// loudness — the record says what was actually asked for and never what
113	    /// a greyed-out popup happened to be sitting on.
114	    ///
115	    /// **The burn-in is gated by that same rule and used not to be**, which
116	    /// broke the sentence above rather than any of the core's: a tick made on
117	    /// an H.264 row and carried across to WAV was written into the record
118	    /// beside a size, an fps and a tier all three deliberately left empty, so
119	    /// a named preset — and the remembered choice, which is this same
120	    /// value — said a file with no picture would carry a burn-in. It is not an
121	    /// override, so nothing downstream ever refused it; `Applies.burnIn`
122	    /// (below) is where it is refused now.
123	    ///
124	    /// The `name` is empty: naming a choice is the Save… item's business.
125	    var currentChoice: ExportChoice {
126	        var choice = ExportChoice(presetID: currentPreset?.id ?? "")
127	        if currentApplies.size {
128	            if isCustomSize {
129	                choice.customSize = [clampedSize(widthField), clampedSize(heightField)]
130	            } else {
131	                let index = sizePopup.indexOfSelectedItem
132	                // The ROW's id, never its index (`ExportChoice.sizeRow`).
133	                // Index 0 is recorded like any other: it is a row a person
134	                // chose, and `sizeOverride()`'s decision to send it as no
135	                // override at all is about the CORE's default and not about
136	                // what the popup was showing.
137	                if index >= 0, index < visibleSizes.count {
138	                    choice.sizeRow = visibleSizes[index].id
139	                }
140	            }
141	        }
142	        choice.fps = currentRate.map { [$0.num, $0.den] }
143	        choice.qualityTier = currentTier?.name
144	        choice.loudness = currentLoudness
145	        choice.inOutRange = rangePopup.indexOfSelectedItem == 1
146	        choice.burnInTimecode = currentApplies.burnIn && recipeOptions.burnInTimecode
147	        choice.encoderSpeed = encoderSpeedChoice.rawValue
148	        choice.audioBits = audioBitsChoice
149	        choice.stems = stemsChoice
150	        return choice
151	    }
152	
153	    /// Writes a stored choice back into the controls. **The order is
154	    /// load-bearing and this method is where it is written down**; every
155	    /// caller — the remembered choice in `loadView`, a preset picked from the
156	    /// popup — goes through here so there is only ever one order.
157	    ///
158	    /// 1. **Format FIRST, before the sizes are listed.** A programmatic
159	    ///    `selectItem` sends no action, so `formatChanged`'s `sizesPreset`
160	    ///    guard never fires and nothing rebuilds on its own; listing after the
161	    ///    pick is what makes the rows this format's rows.
162	    /// 2. **Size AFTER `rebuildSizes()`**, which ends with an unconditional
163	    ///    `sizePopup.selectItem(at: 0)` and would undo a selection made before
164	    ///    it.
165	    /// 3. **A custom LOUDNESS selects "Custom…" first and fills the field
166	    ///    second**, because `syncReadout` overwrites that field from the popup
167	    ///    whenever the popup is not on Custom — and `resolve()` runs one
168	    ///    `syncReadout` after this returns.
169	    /// 4. **`in_out` degrades to "Whole project"** on a document that has no
170	    ///    range: the popup only carries that row when `range != nil`, so
171	    ///    selecting index 1 would select nothing at all.
172	    ///
173	    /// It does NOT resolve. The caller does, once, after the last control has
174	    /// moved — a resolve per control would be six FFI round trips to paint one
175	    /// card.
176	    func apply(_ choice: ExportChoice) {
177	        if let index = presets.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == choice.presetID }) {
178	            formatPopup.selectItem(at: index)
179	        }
180	        rebuildSizes()
181	        applySize(choice)
182	
183	        if let fps = choice.fps, fps.count == 2,
184	            let index = Self.rates.firstIndex(where: { $0.num == fps[0] && $0.den == fps[1] })
185	        {
186	            ratePopup.selectItem(at: index + 1)
187	        } else {
188	            ratePopup.selectItem(at: 0)
189	        }
190	
191	        if let name = choice.qualityTier,
192	            let index = Self.tiers.firstIndex(where: { $0.name == name })
193	        {
194	            qualityPopup.selectItem(at: index + 1)
195	        } else {
196	            qualityPopup.selectItem(at: 0)
197	        }
198	
199	        applyLoudness(choice)
200	        rangePopup.selectItem(at: choice.inOutRange && range != nil ? 1 : 0)
201	        burnInCheckbox.state = choice.burnInTimecode ? .on : .off
202	        applySpeed(choice)
203	        applyAudioBits(choice)
204	        applyStems(choice)
205	    }
206	
207	    /// Step 2, after the listing. A row whose id this format does not offer —
208	    /// a GIF's cap under H.264, or a row `visibleSizes` hid because an earlier
209	    /// row already has its numbers — falls back to the SAME NUMBERS under
210	    /// whatever row does show them, and only then to the format's default.
211	    /// Hiding is a tidiness of the popup's (`visibleSizes`), so a choice of
212	    /// "1080p" on a 1920 × 1080 document has to land on "Document size" rather
213	    /// than be dropped: it is the same export.
214	    private func applySize(_ choice: ExportChoice) {
215	        if let row = choice.sizeRow {
216	            if let index = visibleSizes.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == row }) {
217	                sizePopup.selectItem(at: index)
218	                return
219	            }
220	            if let hidden = sizes.first(where: { $0.id == row }),
221	                let index = visibleSizes.firstIndex(where: {
222	                    $0.width == hidden.width && $0.height == hidden.height
223	                })
224	            {
225	                sizePopup.selectItem(at: index)
226	                return
227	            }
228	            return
229	        }
230	        guard let custom = choice.customSize, custom.count == 2 else { return }
231	        // "Custom…" is the item after the last visible row.
232	        sizePopup.selectItem(at: visibleSizes.count)
233	        widthField.integerValue = custom[0]
234	        heightField.integerValue = custom[1]
235	    }
236	
237	    /// Step 3: the row first, the field second.
238	    private func applyLoudness(_ choice: ExportChoice) {
239	        guard let target = choice.loudness else {
240	            loudnessPopup.selectItem(at: 0)
241	            return
242	        }
243	        if let index = Self.loudnessTargets.firstIndex(of: target) {
244	            loudnessPopup.selectItem(at: index + 1)
245	            return
246	        }
247	        loudnessPopup.selectItem(at: Self.loudnessTargets.count + 1)
248	        loudnessField.doubleValue = target
249	    }
250	
251	    var currentPreset: ExportPreset? {
252	        let index = formatPopup.indexOfSelectedItem
253	        guard index >= 0, index < presets.count else { return nil }
254	        return presets[index]
255	    }
256	
257	    private var currentApplies: Applies { Applies(currentPreset) }
258	
259	    /// True while the Size popup's last item, "Custom…", is chosen — which is
260	    /// also the state of a popup whose listing failed, since Custom is then
261	    /// its only item; harmless, because `resolve()` refuses that case before
262	    /// the fields are read.
263	    var isCustomSize: Bool { sizePopup.indexOfSelectedItem == visibleSizes.count }
264	
265	    /// The frame-rate override, or nil for "Project rate" — and always nil
266	    /// for a preset that has no frames, so a rate picked for a movie cannot
267	    /// follow the user into an audio-only export.
268	    private var currentRate: Fps? {
269	        let index = ratePopup.indexOfSelectedItem - 1
270	        guard currentApplies.frameRate, index >= 0, index < Self.rates.count else { return nil }
271	        return Self.rates[index]
272	    }
273	
274	    /// The quality tier, or nil for "Format default" — and, on the same
275	    /// rule, always nil for a preset that takes no bit rate.
276	    private var currentTier: QualityTier? {
277	        let index = qualityPopup.indexOfSelectedItem - 1
278	        guard currentApplies.quality, index >= 0, index < Self.tiers.count else { return nil }
279	        return Self.tiers[index]
280	    }
281	
282	    /// True while the Loudness popup's last item, "Custom…", is chosen.
283	    var isCustomLoudness: Bool {
284	        loudnessPopup.indexOfSelectedItem == Self.loudnessTargets.count + 1
285	    }
286	
287	    /// The integrated target to normalise to, or nil for "Off" — index 0 of
288	    /// the popup, on the Quality row's established rule that the first item
289	    /// is no override at all. Nil too for a format with no sound, so a target
290	    /// picked for a movie cannot follow the user into a GIF.
291	    private var currentLoudness: Double? {
292	        guard currentApplies.loudness else { return nil }
293	        let index = loudnessPopup.indexOfSelectedItem
294	        if index >= 1, index <= Self.loudnessTargets.count {
295	            return Self.loudnessTargets[index - 1]
296	        }
297	        guard isCustomLoudness, !loudnessField.stringValue.isEmpty else { return nil }
298	        let value = loudnessField.doubleValue
299	        guard value.isFinite else { return nil }
300	        return min(
301	            max(value, Self.loudnessRange.lowerBound), Self.loudnessRange.upperBound)
302	    }
303	
304	    /// The size override, or nil when the Size popup is on its first row.
305	    ///
306	    /// That row is the format's default — the first of the core's list and
307	    /// of `visibleSizes` alike, since nothing precedes it to hide it — and
308	    /// it is sent as NO override rather than as its own numbers so that
309	    /// what ⌘E exports and what the `export` tool exports with no `size`
310	    /// are one code path in the core — the default lives in
311	    /// `export_size.rs`, not in two readings of it. Any other row sends
312	    /// that row's numbers; "Custom…" sends the fields', clamped. Nil too
313	    /// for a format that has no frames, so a size picked for a movie cannot
314	    /// follow the user into an audio-only export.
315	    private func sizeOverride() -> (width: Int, height: Int)? {
316	        guard currentApplies.size else { return nil }
317	        if isCustomSize {
318	            return (clampedSize(widthField), clampedSize(heightField))
319	        }
320	        let index = sizePopup.indexOfSelectedItem
321	        guard index > 0, index < visibleSizes.count else { return nil }
322	        return (visibleSizes[index].width, visibleSizes[index].height)
323	    }
324	
325	    /// The frame the controls are ASKING for: the same numbers `overrides()`
326	    /// sends, plus the fallbacks the core would apply to them.
327	    ///
328	    /// The tiers are computed against this rather than against `resolved`,
329	    /// which still describes the PREVIOUS format at the moment a new one is
330	    /// being resolved — the bit rate would then be one change behind the
331	    /// size it was supposed to be for.
332	    private func requestedFormat() -> (width: Int, height: Int, fps: Fps) {
333	        let canvas = editor?.document?.project.snapshot.canvas ?? CanvasSnapshot()
334	        // No override resolves to the Size popup's first row. The format's
335	        // own cap, then the canvas, stand in for it only when the listing
336	        // failed — the same fallback the core applies to a preset with no
337	        // size (`export.rs`).
338	        var width = sizes.first?.width ?? currentPreset?.width ?? canvas.width
339	        var height = sizes.first?.height ?? currentPreset?.height ?? canvas.height
340	        if let size = sizeOverride() {
341	            width = size.width
342	            height = size.height
343	        }
344	        return (width, height, currentRate ?? canvas.fps)
345	    }
346	
347	    /// The override object, with every key the controls are NOT overriding
348	    /// left out — the same rule the op builders follow, so the core's own
349	    /// defaults apply (§6). Keys are the core's override names in
350	    /// `export.rs` — `width`, `height`, `fps`, `range`, `video_bitrate`,
351	    /// `audio_bitrate`.
352	    private func overrides() -> [String: Any]? {
353	        var overrides: [String: Any] = [:]
354	        let applies = currentApplies
355	        let format = requestedFormat()
356	        if let size = sizeOverride() {
357	            overrides["width"] = size.width
358	            overrides["height"] = size.height
359	        }
360	        if let fps = currentRate {
361	            overrides["fps"] = [fps.num, fps.den]
362	        }
363	        // Bits per second: the unit `export.rs` reads these two overrides in,
364	        // and the one `AVVideoAverageBitRateKey` takes after it. They are
365	        // sent separately because a preset may take one and not the other —
366	        // the audio-only row has no video rate to set, and a frame-sequence
367	        // row has neither.
368	        if let tier = currentTier {
369	            if applies.videoBitrate {
370	                overrides["video_bitrate"] = tier.videoBitsPerSecond(
371	                    width: format.width, height: format.height, fps: format.fps,
372	                    codec: currentPreset?.codec ?? "")
373	            }
374	            if applies.audioBitrate {
375	                overrides["audio_bitrate"] = tier.audioBitsPerSecond
376	            }
377	        }
378	        // Both loudness keys together: the ceiling, fixed at −1 dBTP and
379	        // named in the hint, is the master limiter's (spec §11 AU-27), which
380	        // holds −1 unsent too, so a ceiling goes only beside a target.
381	        if let target = currentLoudness {
382	            overrides["loudness_lufs"] = target
383	            overrides["peak_dbtp"] = Self.peakCeilingDBTP
384	        }
385	        // The core reads the range as ONE nested object (`export.rs`), and
386	        // ignores override keys it does not know — so `start` and `duration`
387	        // spelled at the top level exported the whole project instead of the
388	        // in/out range, silently.
389	        if let picture = dynamicRangeOverride() { overrides["dynamic_range"] = picture }
390	        if let speed = encoderSpeedOverride() { overrides["encoder_speed"] = speed }
391	        if let bits = audioBitsOverride() { overrides["audio_bits"] = bits }
392	        if let stems = stemsOverride() { overrides["stems"] = stems }
393	        if rangePopup.indexOfSelectedItem == 1, let range = range {
394	            overrides["range"] = [
395	                "start": range.start,
396	                "duration": max(0, range.end - range.start),
397	            ]
398	        }
399	        return overrides.isEmpty ? nil : overrides
400	    }
401	
402	    private func clampedSize(_ field: NSTextField) -> Int {
403	        min(max(field.integerValue, Self.sizeRange.lowerBound), Self.sizeRange.upperBound)
404	    }
405	
406	    /// Rewrites the readout, the footnote, the controls' enablement and the
407	    /// Export button from `resolved`. The size fields follow the core while
408	    /// a row of the Size popup owns the size, which is what makes "Custom…"
409	    /// readable: pick it and the fields already hold the numbers to edit.
410	    ///
411	    /// Enablement comes from the FORMAT rather than from `resolved`, so a
412	    /// refused resolve leaves the controls where they were instead of
413	    /// greying out the very one that has to be changed to fix it.
414	    private func syncReadout() {
415	        let applies = currentApplies
416	        let custom = isCustomSize
417	        // A popup whose listing failed holds nothing to choose, and the one
418	        // control that can put a size back is the Format popup, so the size
419	        // controls grey out with it — the exception to the rule in the doc
420	        // comment above, for the one refusal no size can fix.
421	        let listed = sizesError == nil
422	        sizePopup.isEnabled = applies.size && listed
423	        for field in [widthField, heightField] {
424	            field.isEnabled = applies.size && listed && custom
425	            field.textColor = field.isEnabled ? DS.textStrong : DS.textMuted
426	        }
427	        ratePopup.isEnabled = applies.frameRate
428	        qualityPopup.isEnabled = applies.quality
429	        syncQualityTitles(applies)
430	        loudnessPopup.isEnabled = applies.loudness
431	        loudnessField.isEnabled = applies.loudness && isCustomLoudness
432	        loudnessField.textColor = loudnessField.isEnabled ? DS.textStrong : DS.textMuted
433	        if !isCustomLoudness {
434	            // The field mirrors the row that is chosen, exactly as the size
435	            // fields mirror the core's answer, so picking "Custom…" starts
436	            // from the number that was in force a moment before. "Off" has no
437	            // number of its own, so it shows the first target — the one
438	            // Custom is most likely to be an adjustment of.
439	            loudnessField.doubleValue = currentLoudness ?? Self.loudnessTargets[0]
440	        }
441	        // The last control on the card, and the last one to be gated: the
442	        // burn-in stayed live on the three audio-only rows, alone among the
443	        // format-dependent controls, offering to write a timecode into a file
444	        // with no picture to write it into.
445	        burnInCheckbox.isEnabled = applies.burnIn
446	        syncDynamicRange(applies)
447	        syncSpeed(applies)
448	        syncAudioBits(applies)
449	        syncStems(applies)
450	
451	        guard let settings = resolved else {
452	            summaryLabel.stringValue = resolveError ?? "These settings are not available."
453	            summaryLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
454	            footnote.stringValue = ""
455	            footnote.toolTip = nil
456	            exportButton?.isEnabled = false
457	            return
458	        }
459	        if !custom {
460	            widthField.integerValue = settings.width
461	            heightField.integerValue = settings.height
462	        }
463	        summaryLabel.textColor = DS.textMuted
464	        summaryLabel.stringValue = summary(for: settings)
465	        footnote.stringValue = footnoteText(for: settings)
466	        footnote.toolTip = footnote.stringValue
467	        exportButton?.isEnabled = settings.duration > 0
468	    }
469	
470	    /// Re-titles the tier rows with the rate each would ask for at the size
471	    /// and frame rate now chosen. "High" on its own says nothing; "High ·
472	    /// 8.0 Mbps" is the control's actual promise, and it has to move when
473	    /// the frame it is a rate for moves.
474	    private func syncQualityTitles(_ applies: Applies) {
475	        let format = requestedFormat()
476	        let codec = currentPreset?.codec ?? ""
477	        for (index, tier) in Self.tiers.enumerated() {
478	            guard let item = qualityPopup.item(at: index + 1) else { continue }
479	            if applies.videoBitrate {
480	                let rate = tier.videoBitsPerSecond(
481	                    width: format.width, height: format.height, fps: format.fps, codec: codec)
482	                let soft = applies.softCap ? "usually ≤ " : ""   // spec §11 CX-13
483	                item.title = "\(tier.name) · \(soft)\(Self.rateText(rate))"
484	            } else if applies.audioBitrate {
485	                item.title = "\(tier.name) · \(Self.rateText(tier.audioBitsPerSecond))"
486	            } else {
487	                item.title = tier.name
488	            }
489	        }
490	    }
491	
492	    /// The one-line description of what the file will contain.
493	    private func summary(for settings: ExportSettings) -> String {
494	        if settings.isAudioOnly {
495	            // Milliseconds rather than frames, and no rate in the line: audio
496	            // has no frames, which is the same reason the rate popup is
497	            // greyed out for this preset.
498	            let duration = ReelTime.format(settings.duration, fps: settings.fps, frames: false)
499	            return "Audio only · \(duration)"
500	        }
501	        let duration = ReelTime.format(settings.duration, fps: settings.fps, frames: true)
502	        var text = "\(settings.width) × \(settings.height) · \(settings.fps.displayName) fps · "
503	            + duration
504	        if Self.isFrameSequence(container: settings.container) {
505	            // What a GIF or an APNG costs is frames, not seconds — and it
506	            // carries no audio however much of it the timeline has, which is
507	            // worth saying before the export rather than after it.
508	            text += " · \(settings.sequenceFrameCount ?? 0) frames, no audio"
509	        }
510	        // A bundled encoder's estimate (spec §11 CX-18 (9)).
511	        if let line = ExportEncoderCosts.sheetLine(for: settings) { text += "\n" + line }
512	        return text
513	    }
514	
515	    /// The footnote over the buttons: the codec, the container, and the rates
516	    /// the CORE resolved — never the ones the tier asked for, and not filtered by
517	    /// what the sheet thinks applies, since a preset is free to carry a rate
518	    /// of its own that no control here offered.
519	    ///
520	    /// The distinction matters because `export.rs` drops override keys it
521	    /// does not know, silently (the same trap the range comment above names).
522	    /// A tier picked against a core that has no bit-rate overrides has to
523	    /// read as "the format's own rate" rather than let the popup imply a
524	    /// number the file will not have.
525	    private func footnoteText(for settings: ExportSettings) -> String {
526	        var parts = [settings.codec.uppercased()]
527	        let container = settings.container.uppercased()
528	        // A frame-sequence preset's codec IS its container: "GIF · GIF".
529	        if container != parts[0] { parts.append(container) }
530	        if let speed = settings.encoderSpeed { parts.append(speed.menuName) }
531	        if settings.audioBits == 24 { parts.append("24-bit") }
532	        if case let n = settings.stems.count, n > 0 { parts.append(n == 1 ? "1 stem" : "\(n) stems") }
533	        if let rate = settings.videoBitrate {
534	            // A bundled encoder's rate is a soft cap (spec §11 CX-13).
535	            parts.append((settings.writer == nil ? "" : "usually ≤ ") + Self.rateText(rate))
536	        }
537	        if let rate = settings.audioBitrate {
538	            parts.append("\(Self.rateText(rate)) audio")
539	        }
540	        if currentTier != nil, settings.videoBitrate == nil, settings.audioBitrate == nil {
541	            parts.append("format's own rate")
542	        }
543	        // The core's echo, not the popup's row: a build whose
544	        // `export_settings` has never heard of `loudness_lufs` drops the key
545	        // silently, and the footnote must not then promise a normalisation
546	        // the file will not have.
547	        if let target = settings.loudnessLufs {
548	            parts.append(
549	                String(format: "%g LUFS", target).replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−"))
550	        }
551	        // Whether the ENCODING carries a fourth channel — the core's own
552	        // answer for this row (`ExportSettings.alpha`), never a reading of the
553	        // canvas. It is the one place the sheet says which format keeps a
554	        // transparent background, and it is a POSITIVE claim only: the rows
555	        // that answer false are not enumerated here, because the flag says
556	        // what the settings object says and the footnote's whole rule is that
557	        // it reports the core rather than the popup.
558	        if settings.alpha { parts.append("alpha") }
559	        return parts.joined(separator: " · ")
560	    }
561	}
562	
563	// MARK: - The control `Applies` was missing
564	
565	extension ExportSheetController.Applies {
566	    /// Whether the picked format can take a burn-in.
567	    ///
568	    /// It was the one FORMAT-DEPENDENT control on the card that `Applies` did
569	    /// not answer for, and it stayed live on the three audio-only rows while
570	    /// Size, Frame rate and Quality greyed out around it — a checkbox
571	    /// promising to write a timecode into a file with no picture. The tick was
572	    /// inert on the FILE (`ExporterWriter.addVideo` returns at
573	    /// `settings.isAudioOnly`, so an audio-only export composes no frame at
574	    /// all), which is why nothing downstream ever complained; what it was not
575	    /// inert on is the RECORD, because `currentChoice` wrote it into a saved
576	    /// preset and into the remembered choice beside a size, an fps and a tier
577	    /// that same method had deliberately left empty.
578	    ///
579	    /// It answers `size`, and that is the definition rather than a
580	    /// coincidence: a burn-in is a TEXT LAYER drawn into the picture, so it
581	    /// applies exactly where a size does — both are `Applies`' own
582	    /// `hasVideo`. Spelled through `size` rather than through the preset
583	    /// because `hasVideo` is `private` to `ExportSheetOptions.swift`, and a
584	    /// second reading of `!preset.audioOnly` is precisely the drift `Applies`
585	    /// exists to prevent; it belongs beside its four siblings the next time
586	    /// that file is open.
587	    var burnIn: Bool { size }
588	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

     3	/// SVT-AV1 v4.2.0, the `av1` row's encoder (spec §11 CX-2, CX-4, CX-12, CX-14): one handle
     4	/// per export, configured once, fed video-range I010 pictures and drained of packets.
     5	///
     6	/// **Owned by one serial queue.** `ExportEncodePump`'s encode queue makes every call after
     7	/// `init` — `send`, `sendEndOfStream`, `nextPacket` and the `deinit` — so the handle is
     8	/// never touched from two threads; SVT runs its own worker threads behind it.
     9	///
    10	/// **The configuration** (CX-12 (2), (3); CX-13): the sheet's speed as SVT's preset (8, 6 or
    11	/// 4), capped CRF — a constant quality matched to HEVC's at the cap, which is the settings'
    12	/// rate or HEVC's 0.07 bits per pixel per frame — a closed GOP (`SVT_AV1_KF_REFRESH`) with a
    13	/// keyframe at least every 2 s, 10-bit Main 4:2:0, and the picture's primaries, transfer
    14	/// and matrix in video range written into the sequence header (CX-14 (4)): BT.709's for the
    15	/// SDR picture, BT.2020 with HLG or PQ for the HDR ones. On PQ alone, HD-5's fixed mastering
    16	/// display and content light level, which SVT writes as metadata OBUs on each KEY_FRAME
    17	/// (CX-14 (5)).
    18	final class SVTAV1Encoder: ExportVideoEncoder {
    19	    /// A packet as SVT answered it (`ExportEncodedPacket`): its bytes with the temporal
    20	    /// delimiters still in (`containerBytes` strips them), the key flag a KEY_FRAME.
    21	    typealias Packet = ExportEncodedPacket
    22	
    23	    let name = "SVT-AV1"
    24	
    25	    /// The sequence header OBU (`svt_av1_enc_stream_header`), the `av1C` record's source.
    26	    let sequenceHeader: Data
    27	
    28	    private var handle: UnsafeMutablePointer<EbComponentType>?
    29	    /// Set after the first failed call: nothing more is asked of the handle but its teardown.
    30	    private var broken = false
    31	
    32	    init(
    33	        width: Int, height: Int, fps: Fps, bitsPerSecond: Int, speed: EncoderSpeed,
    34	        picture: ExportAV1Picture
    35	    ) throws {
    36	        _ = Self.installLogCallback
    37	        var config = EbSvtAv1EncConfiguration()
    38	        var opened: UnsafeMutablePointer<EbComponentType>?
    39	        try Self.check(svt_av1_enc_init_handle(&opened, &config), "svt_av1_enc_init_handle")
    40	        guard let opened else {
    41	            throw Exporter.ExportError.failed("SVT-AV1 could not start: no handle was made.")
    42	        }
    43	        config.enc_mode = speed.svtPreset
    44	        config.source_width = UInt32(clamping: width)
    45	        config.source_height = UInt32(clamping: height)
    46	        config.frame_rate_numerator = UInt32(clamping: fps.num)
    47	        config.frame_rate_denominator = UInt32(clamping: fps.den)
    48	        config.encoder_bit_depth = 10
    49	        config.encoder_color_format = EB_YUV420
    50	        config.profile = MAIN_PROFILE
    51	        // Capped CRF (CX-13): what SVT's own `--crf` sets, and the cap as `max_bit_rate`.
    52	        let cap = min(max(1, bitsPerSecond), Self.maxCap)
    53	        config.rate_control_mode = UInt8(SVT_AV1_RC_MODE_CQP_OR_CRF.rawValue)
    54	        config.aq_mode = 2
    55	        config.qp = Self.crf(speed: speed, bitsPerPixel: Double(cap)
    56	            / (Double(max(1, width * height)) * (fps.double > 0 ? fps.double : 30)))
    57	        config.max_bit_rate = UInt32(cap)
    58	        // SVT-AV1 v4.2.0's own default (`EbSvtAv1Enc.h`, `enc_settings.c`): a soft cap that
    59	        // hard footage may exceed, the owner's "quality first" (CX-13 (1)).
    60	        config.mbr_over_shoot_pct = 50
   165	        guard let handle, !broken else { throw Self.stopped }
   166	        var out: UnsafeMutablePointer<EbBufferHeaderType>?
   167	        let answer = svt_av1_enc_get_packet(handle, &out, wait ? 1 : 0)
   168	        if answer == EB_NoErrorEmptyQueue { return nil }
   169	        try record(answer, "svt_av1_enc_get_packet")

   171	        defer { svt_av1_enc_release_out_buffer(&out) }

   179	    // MARK: - The rate (CX-13)
   180	
   181	    /// SVT-AV1's largest `max_bit_rate`, 100,000 kb/s.
   182	    private static let maxCap = 100_000_000
   183	
   184	    /// CX-13 (3)'s calibration, CX-14 (6)'s at 10 bits: at each cap in bits per pixel per
   185	    /// frame (the Quality tiers' and "Format default"'s at 1080p30), the highest CRF at which
   186	    /// each speed reached VMAF ≥ HEVC's at that rate on every calibration clip — the spike's
   187	    /// three 8-bit clips against 8-bit HEVC, and the owner's 55 s clip through this app at
   188	    /// 10 bits against `hevc_10bit` — Faster, Balanced, Smaller file.
   189	    private static let calibration: [(bitsPerPixel: Double, crf: [EncoderSpeed: Double])] = [
   190	        (0.0386, [.faster: 36, .balanced: 36, .smaller: 36]),
   191	        (0.0579, [.faster: 26, .balanced: 28, .smaller: 28]),
   192	        (0.0700, [.faster: 22, .balanced: 24, .smaller: 24]),
   193	        (0.0772, [.faster: 20, .balanced: 24, .smaller: 24]),
   194	        (0.1157, [.faster: 12, .balanced: 16, .smaller: 16]),
   195	    ]
   196	
   197	    /// The CRF for `speed` at a cap of `bitsPerPixel`: linear between the calibrated points,
   198	    /// rounded down, and the end point's beyond either end (`ExportRateTable`).
   199	    static func crf(speed: EncoderSpeed, bitsPerPixel: Double) -> UInt32 {
   200	        ExportRateTable.value(
   201	            at: bitsPerPixel,
   202	            points: calibration.map { (bitsPerPixel: $0.bitsPerPixel, value: $0.crf[speed] ?? 32) })
   203	    }

   205	    // MARK: - Errors and the log
   206	
   207	    private static let stopped = Exporter.ExportError.failed(
   208	        "SVT-AV1 stopped after an earlier error.")
   209	
   210	    private func record(_ answer: EbErrorType, _ step: String) throws {
   211	        guard answer != EB_ErrorNone else { return }
   212	        broken = true
   213	        throw Exporter.ExportError.failed("SVT-AV1 failed: \(step) answered \(Self.hex(answer)).")
   214	    }
   215	
   216	    private static func check(_ answer: EbErrorType, _ step: String) throws {
   217	        guard answer != EB_ErrorNone else { return }
   218	        throw Exporter.ExportError.failed(
   219	            "SVT-AV1 could not start: \(step) answered \(hex(answer)).")
   220	    }
   221	
   222	    private static func hex(_ answer: EbErrorType) -> String {
   223	        "0x" + String(UInt32(bitPattern: answer.rawValue), radix: 16)
   224	    }
   225	
   226	    /// SVT's log through its callback (spec §11 CX-12 (6)), installed once per process before
   227	    /// the first `svt_av1_enc_init_handle`, which finalises the library's logging: info and
   228	    /// debug dropped, warnings and errors as `SVT-AV1: …` lines in the system log.
   229	    private static let installLogCallback: Void = {
   230	        svt_av1_set_log_callback({ _, level, _, format, arguments in
   231	            guard level.rawValue >= 0, level.rawValue <= SVT_AV1_LOG_WARN.rawValue, let format,
   232	                let arguments
   233	            else { return }
   234	            var text = [CChar](repeating: 0, count: 1024)
   235	            _ = vsnprintf(&text, text.count, format, arguments)
   236	            let line = String(cString: text).trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
   237	            NSLog("SVT-AV1: %@", line)
   238	        }, nil)
   239	    }()
   240	}

     3	/// libvpx v1.17.0's VP9, the `vp9_webm` row's encoder (spec §11 CX-3, CX-4, CX-16): one context
     4	/// per export, configured once, fed video-range pictures and drained of packets.
     5	///
     6	/// **Owned by one serial queue.** `ExportEncodePump`'s encode queue makes every call after
     7	/// `init` — `send`, `sendEndOfStream`, `nextPacket` and the `deinit` — so the context is never
     8	/// touched from two threads; libvpx runs its own worker threads (`g_threads`, row-mt) behind
     9	/// it.
    10	///
    11	/// **The configuration** (CX-16 (2)–(7)): `VPX_DL_GOOD_QUALITY` at cpu-used 4 with row-mt, the
    12	/// one speed (CX-3); the depth by picture — Profile 0, 8-bit I420 for `sdr`, Profile 2, 10-bit
    13	/// I010 (`VPX_IMG_FMT_I42016`) for `hlg` and `pq` — with the matrix's colour space in studio
    14	/// range; a keyframe at least every 2 s (`kf_max_dist` ⌊2·fps⌋); a 25-frame lag with alt-refs,
    15	/// two log2 tile columns; and capped constant quality: `VPX_CQ` at the table's CQ level with
    16	/// the cap as the target, libvpx's own 25 % overshoot. VP9's bitstream carries no transfer, so
    17	/// the WebM `Colour` is the picture's only label (`ExportWebMLayout`).
    18	///
    19	/// **Packets.** libvpx packs a hidden alt-ref into the next shown frame's superframe, so each
    20	/// packet is one shown frame at the pts (the frame index, timebase 1/fps) it was sent with.
    21	/// They are collected after each `vpx_codec_encode` into `pending`; the end of stream encodes
    22	/// NULL until no packet comes out.
    23	///
    24	/// **`vp9_alpha_webm`** (CX-17 (3), (4)) runs two of these (`VP9AlphaEncoder`): the picture as
    25	/// above, and the alpha (`Plane.alpha`), which encodes the frame's alpha planes at constant
    26	/// quality (`VPX_Q` at `alphaCQLevel(pixels:)`, banded by size) in full range. Both take a
    27	/// `keyInterval`: `kf_min_dist` = `kf_max_dist` = it, and every frame whose index is a
    28	/// multiple of it is forced a key, so the two streams' keys fall on the same frames.
    29	final class VP9Encoder: ExportVideoEncoder {
    30	    /// Which planes of a frame an encoder encodes: the picture's (Y, Cb, Cr) or the alpha's
    31	    /// (`I010Frame.alphaOffset`, with the constant chroma at `alphaChromaOffset`).
    32	    enum Plane {
    33	        case picture, alpha
    34	    }
    35	
    36	    let name = "libvpx"
    37	
    38	    private var context = vpx_codec_ctx_t()
    39	    private var image = vpx_image_t()
    40	    private var open = false
    41	    private let format: vpx_img_fmt_t
    42	    private let bytesPerSample: Int
    43	    private let bitDepth: Int
    44	    /// The packets libvpx has answered and the pump has not yet taken, oldest first.
    45	    private var pending: [ExportEncodedPacket] = []
    46	    private var flushing = false
    47	    private var drained = false
    48	    /// Set after the first failed call: nothing more is asked of the context but its teardown.
    49	    private var broken = false
    50	    private let plane: Plane
    51	    /// The forced key interval in frames, nil for CX-16 (6)'s automatic keys.
    52	    private let keyInterval: Int?
    53	
    54	    init(
    55	        width: Int, height: Int, fps: Fps, bitsPerSecond: Int, picture: ExportAV1Picture,
    56	        plane: Plane = .picture, keyInterval: Int? = nil
    57	    ) throws {
    58	        self.plane = plane
    59	        self.keyInterval = keyInterval.map { max(1, $0) }
    60	        let depth = Self.bitDepth(for: picture)
    61	        bitDepth = depth
    62	        bytesPerSample = depth > 8 ? 2 : 1
    63	        format = depth > 8 ? VPX_IMG_FMT_I42016 : VPX_IMG_FMT_I420
    64	        var config = vpx_codec_enc_cfg_t()
    65	        try Self.check(
    66	            vpx_codec_enc_config_default(vpx_codec_vp9_cx(), &config, 0),
    67	            "vpx_codec_enc_config_default", context: nil)
    68	        config.g_w = UInt32(clamping: width)
    69	        config.g_h = UInt32(clamping: height)
    70	        // Timebase 1/fps: a frame's pts is its index and its duration 1.
    71	        config.g_timebase = vpx_rational(
    72	            num: Int32(clamping: max(1, fps.den)), den: Int32(clamping: max(1, fps.num)))
    73	        config.g_threads = UInt32(clamping: ProcessInfo.processInfo.activeProcessorCount)
    74	        config.g_pass = VPX_RC_ONE_PASS
    75	        config.g_lag_in_frames = 25
    76	        // The depth (CX-16 (3)): libvpx's `validate_config` refuses a depth above 8 at a
    77	        // profile below 2.
    78	        config.g_profile = depth > 8 ? 2 : 0
    79	        config.g_bit_depth = depth > 8 ? VPX_BITS_10 : VPX_BITS_8
    80	        config.g_input_bit_depth = UInt32(depth)
    81	        // Capped CQ (CX-16 (7)): the cap in kb/s as the target, libvpx's default
    82	        // over- and undershoot (25 / 25).
    83	        let cap = max(1, bitsPerSecond)
    84	        // The alpha is constant quality with no cap (CX-17 (3)).
    85	        config.rc_end_usage = plane == .alpha ? VPX_Q : VPX_CQ
    86	        config.rc_target_bitrate = UInt32(max(1, (Double(cap) / 1000).rounded()))
    87	        // A keyframe at least every 2 s (CX-16 (6)).
    88	        let perSecond = fps.den > 0 ? Double(fps.num) / Double(fps.den) : 30
    89	        config.kf_mode = VPX_KF_AUTO
    90	        config.kf_min_dist = 0
    91	        config.kf_max_dist = UInt32(max(1, (2 * perSecond).rounded(.down)))
    92	        // Keys at fixed frames (CX-17 (4)), the two alpha row's streams alike.
    93	        if let interval = self.keyInterval {
    94	            config.kf_min_dist = UInt32(clamping: interval)
    95	            config.kf_max_dist = UInt32(clamping: interval)
    96	        }
    97	        let flags = depth > 8 ? vpx_codec_flags_t(VPX_CODEC_USE_HIGHBITDEPTH) : 0
    98	        try Self.check(
    99	            framejob_vpx_vp9_enc_init(&context, &config, flags), "vpx_codec_enc_init",
   100	            context: nil)
   101	        open = true
   102	        let pixels = Double(max(1, width * height)) * (perSecond > 0 ? perSecond : 30)
   103	        let range = plane == .alpha ? VPX_CR_FULL_RANGE : VPX_CR_STUDIO_RANGE
   104	        let level = plane == .alpha
   105	            ? Self.alphaCQLevel(pixels: width * height)
   106	            : Int32(Self.cqLevel(bitDepth: depth, bitsPerPixel: Double(cap) / pixels))
   107	        let controls: [(vp8e_enc_control_id, Int32)] = [
   108	            (VP8E_SET_CPUUSED, 4),
   109	            (VP9E_SET_ROW_MT, 1),
   110	            (VP8E_SET_ENABLEAUTOALTREF, 1),
   111	            (VP9E_SET_TILE_COLUMNS, 2),
   112	            (VP9E_SET_FRAME_PARALLEL_DECODING, 0),
   113	            (VP8E_SET_CQ_LEVEL, level),
   114	            (VP9E_SET_COLOR_SPACE,
   115	             Int32((picture == .sdr ? VPX_CS_BT_709 : VPX_CS_BT_2020).rawValue)),
   116	            (VP9E_SET_COLOR_RANGE, Int32(range.rawValue)),
   117	        ]
   118	        for (id, value) in controls {
   119	            try Self.check(
   120	                framejob_vpx_control_int(&context, Int32(id.rawValue), value),
   121	                "vpx_codec_control \(id.rawValue)", context: &context)
   122	        }
   123	        // The image header `send` points at each frame's planes: 4:2:0 at the export size,
   124	        // the picture's colour space in studio range, the alpha in full (no storage of its
   125	        // own).
   126	        image.fmt = format
   127	        image.cs = picture == .sdr ? VPX_CS_BT_709 : VPX_CS_BT_2020
   128	        image.range = range
   129	        image.w = UInt32(clamping: width)
   130	        image.h = UInt32(clamping: height)

     3	/// The `av1_webm` row's sound (spec §11 CX-7, CX-15 (5)): the export's 16-bit interleaved
     4	/// 48 kHz stereo mix (`ExportAudioMaster`'s output, in `ExportWriter.decodedAudioSettings`'
     5	/// shape) encoded to Opus by AudioToolbox's `AVAudioConverter`, in 20 ms packets.
     6	///
     7	/// **A 960-frame FIFO** sits in front of the converter, so it is handed whole packets'
     8	/// worth of frames whatever size the reader's buffers come in; packet k is timed at
     9	/// k × 20 ms. **The pre-skip** is the converter's `primeInfo.leadingFrames` (312 measured),
    10	/// which the WebM's OpusHead and CodecDelay carry. **The end:** `finish()` feeds `preSkip`
    11	/// frames of silence through the FIFO (and zeros to a whole packet), then the end of stream,
    12	/// so the packets cover every frame fed — packets × 960 ≥ pre-skip + frames fed — and the
    13	/// writer cuts the surplus with DiscardPadding.
    14	///
    15	/// One instance per export, used only on the WebM writer's audio queue.
    16	final class ExportOpusEncoder {
    17	    /// The AAC rows' own default (spec §11 CX-15 (5)).
    18	    static let defaultBitRate = 192_000
    19	    static let framesPerPacket = 960
    20	    private static let channels = 2
    21	
    22	    let preSkip: Int
    23	    /// Frames handed to the FIFO, silence from `finish` included.
    24	    private(set) var framesFed = 0
    25	    /// Packets the converter has answered.
    26	    private(set) var packetsOut = 0
    27	
    28	    private let converter: AVAudioConverter
    29	    private let inputFormat: AVAudioFormat
    30	    private let outputFormat: AVAudioFormat
    31	    /// Interleaved samples not yet handed to the converter.
    32	    private var fifo: [Int16] = []
    33	    private var finished = false
    34	
    35	    /// A converter at `bitRate` bits per second, snapped to the nearest rate it offers.
    36	    init(bitRate: Int) throws {
    37	        var opus = AudioStreamBasicDescription(
    38	            mSampleRate: 48_000, mFormatID: kAudioFormatOpus, mFormatFlags: 0,
    39	            mBytesPerPacket: 0, mFramesPerPacket: UInt32(Self.framesPerPacket),
    40	            mBytesPerFrame: 0, mChannelsPerFrame: UInt32(Self.channels), mBitsPerChannel: 0,
    41	            mReserved: 0)
    42	        guard let input = AVAudioFormat(
    43	            commonFormat: .pcmFormatInt16, sampleRate: 48_000,
    44	            channels: AVAudioChannelCount(Self.channels), interleaved: true),
    45	            let output = AVAudioFormat(streamDescription: &opus),
    46	            let converter = AVAudioConverter(from: input, to: output)
    47	        else {
    48	            throw Exporter.ExportError.failed("The Opus encoder could not be started.")
    49	        }
    50	        let offered = (converter.applicableEncodeBitRates ?? []).map(\.intValue)
    51	        if let nearest = offered.min(by: { abs($0 - bitRate) < abs($1 - bitRate) }) {
    52	            converter.bitRate = nearest
    53	        } else {
    54	            converter.bitRate = max(1, bitRate)
    55	        }
    56	        self.converter = converter
    57	        inputFormat = input
    58	        outputFormat = output
    59	        preSkip = Int(converter.primeInfo.leadingFrames)
    60	    }
    61	
    62	    @available(*, unavailable) required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
    63	        fatalError("ExportOpusEncoder does not support NSCoder")
    64	    }
    65	
    66	    /// Feeds `sample`'s frames and answers every packet the converter makes of whole
    67	    /// 960-frame chunks. The frames are counted from the buffer's BYTES (4 a frame), so a
    68	    /// buffer of any length — one cut short at the range's end included — goes through the
    69	    /// FIFO whole. Throws, in a sentence, when its bytes are not a whole number of 16-bit
    70	    /// stereo frames, when they cannot be read, or when the converter fails.
    71	    func encode(_ sample: CMSampleBuffer) throws -> [Data] {
    72	        guard let block = CMSampleBufferGetDataBuffer(sample) else {
    73	            guard CMSampleBufferGetNumSamples(sample) == 0 else {
    74	                throw Exporter.ExportError.failed("A sound buffer could not be read for Opus.")
    75	            }
    76	            return []
    77	        }
    78	        let bytes = CMBlockBufferGetDataLength(block)
    79	        let frameBytes = Self.channels * MemoryLayout<Int16>.size
    80	        guard bytes % frameBytes == 0 else {

            throw Exporter.ExportError.emptyTimeline

        guard videoReader.canAdd(videoOutput) else {
            throw Exporter.ExportError.failed("The composition could not be read for export.")
        }

        let hasAudio = !built.composition.tracks(withMediaType: .audio).isEmpty

                bitRate: settings.audioBitrate.map { max(1, $0) }

            settings: settings, range: range, codec: pump.webmCodec, picture: pump.picture,
            preSkip: opus?.preSkip, chapters: chapters

    }

content.content:
Starts writing the timeline to a file and answers AT ONCE with {export_id, path, status} — ⌘E, the export sheet's six controls (format, size, frame rate, quality, loudness, range) in the sheet's own vocabulary, all but the frame rate — this exports at the document's rate, or on gif and apng at the format's own rate (12.5 and 25 fps). The export is a job in the Export Queue, run one at a time behind any other export already there; status is queued or running. An av1, av1_webm or vp9_webm job also waits while the app's other AV1 and VP9 exports would hold more than a quarter of this Mac's memory with it, and a later job may run first meanwhile (export_status's waiting says so). Follow it with export_status, which never waits — call it again after a pause until status is done, failed or cancelled — and stop it with cancel_export. The export_id lasts until Frame Job quits. Every refusal comes back from this call, before anything is queued: a bad argument, a missing folder, and a graphic clip whose module does not compile; a failure while writing comes back from export_status, failed with its reason (a graphic that fails during the export stops it with no file left, naming the graphic and the frame). The preset is the ENCODING only and the size a separate choice defaulting to the document's own, or on gif and apng to the format's cap; the core resolves both into concrete settings (container, codec, size, rate, range) and hands them to the same exporter the sheet uses, so an agent export and a menu export cannot disagree. An existing file at the path is replaced, and the container's extension is added when the path has none. In an HLG project (set_canvas output) hevc_10bit, av1, av1_webm, vp9_webm, prores_422 and prores_4444 write HLG unless dynamic_range says pq or sdr, and every other video preset writes the project's SDR version. What the finished file holds is export_status's done answer.

Omit for -1 (the sheet's fixed value); 0 is the loosest, and there is no off. Legal with or without loudness_lufs. How far the limiter turned the hottest peak down is the result's limited_db."
},
"audio_bits": {
"description": "audio_wav's and audio_aiff's bit depth \u2014 the sheet's Bit depth popup: 16 (the default) or 24, rounded once from the float mix, never dithered. Refused on every other preset (ProRes keeps 16).",

"enum": [
16,
24
]
},
"preset": {
"type": "string",
"description": "Export preset id \u2014 one per encoding, a container and a codec with no size of its own (that is size's). h264 is what the export sheet opens on. Four rows keep a transparent canvas transparent: prores_4444, hevc_alpha and vp9_alpha_webm (the movie rows \u2014 see size, which constrains them) and apng. gif is not one of them: it can show a transparent pixel but has no alpha channel, so nothing partial survives it. prores_422, prores_4444 and hevc_10bit keep the compositor's 16-bit frames at 10 bits (ProRes 4444 at 12); h264, hevc and hevc_alpha are 8-bit. av1 is AV1 in an MP4 with AAC and av1_webm the same AV1 in a WebM with Opus, both 10-bit, encoded by the bundled SVT-AV1 at encoder_speed; Macs before M3 cannot play them back. vp9_webm is VP9 in a WebM with Opus from the bundled libvpx, at one speed: 8-bit (Profile 0) for an SDR picture, 10-bit (Profile 2) for HLG and PQ. vp9_alpha_webm is that VP9 with its alpha, always 8-bit (the SDR version in an HLG project), the transparent movie Chrome and Firefox play; Safari's is hevc_alpha. Pass a wrong one and the error lists them all."
},
"dynamic_range": {
"description": "An HDR (HLG) project's picture on hevc_10bit, av1, av1_webm, vp9_webm, prores_422 and prores_4444 \u2014 the sheet's Dynamic Range popup: hlg (the default; BT.2100 HLG, no Dolby Vision), pq (HDR10: BT.2100 PQ at 1,000 cd/m\u00b2, mastering display P3-D65 0.005\u20131,000 cd/m\u00b2, MaxCLL 1,000, MaxFALL 0) or sdr (the SDR version). Every other video preset (vp9_alpha_webm too) writes the SDR version; hlg and pq are refused there and in an SDR project, where sdr changes nothing.",
"type": "string",
"enum": [

"pq",
"sdr"
]

"type": "number",

"description": "Normalise the whole mix to this integrated loudness, in LUFS \u2014 the sheet's Loudness popup, whose rows are -14 (streaming), -16 (podcast) and -23 (EBU R 128 broadcast). The export measures itself first and then applies ONE gain to everything, solved through the master limiter every export runs at peak_dbtp, so the file lands on the target and its loudest peaks are limited rather than the whole mix capped. Omit not to normalise: the export still measures, still limits at the ceiling and still reports. Ignored where there is no sound to measure (gif, apng)."
},

Omit for the document size or the image format's cap; a wrong id's error lists the ids.
